items.t: times. The blessed litany (wird) is completed, with the praise of God and His help.
Chapter 16 (al-bāb al-sādis ʿashar): On the Most Beautiful Names of God and on their beneficial, tried-and- tested awfāq [190]

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success — that this is the first […], well-guarded, a hidden [pearl], issuing forth from the valley of purity to the intimate friends of fidelity and to the elect of purity: those who ride upon the necks of the winds of longing, who fly upon the wings of the draughts of [spiritual] tasting toward the understanding of these sciences of divine bestowal /fol. 126v./ and of the understandings that come by effusion, and the musk-scented seals, and the inscriptions of [divine] opening, and the Indian ciphers, and the subtleties of the letters, and the gnoses of number, and the luminous names, and the realities of the Furqān, and the spiritual concordances. May God bring me and you into the garden of secrets and the orchard of lights. I say — and from God comes success, and from Him unveiling and verification: Know — may God bring me and you into the Frequented House, and grant me and you accord with the companions of the Unrolled Parchment — that the names of God, exalted is He, considered with respect to what of them has come in the Book and in the Sunna, whether in the form of a noun or in the form of a verb from which, however, a noun is derived; and with respect to what the people of unveiling apply to Him by way of the realities of the names, of whatever is an attribute of perfection — are exceedingly many. For if we count such [pairs] as al-Qāhir (the Subduer) and al-Qahhār (the All-Subduing), and al-Shākir (the Thankful) and al-Shakūr (the Most Thankful), as two names, they come near to reaching three hundred; and it is said that they reach six thousand. The purpose in this indication is only brevity, and a hinting toward this hidden science and this treasured secret, so as to alert him who seeks it. And whoever has been allotted anything of a share in it, let him hasten to cut through the obstacles of wayfaring, and to divest himself of the blameworthy traits of character and the basest of them, and to adorn himself with the praiseworthy and fairest of them, which are the character of the Real, glorified and exalted. Then you will attain to the like of these matters here set down; for the taking of this science is [otherwise] a dead thing received from a dead thing. God, exalted is He, said: No soul knows what comfort of the eyes has been hidden away for them, as a recompense for what they used to do (Q 32:17).

For that reason I have set myself to speak upon the ninety-nine names; and I have thought fit to adduce them first, under a condition, as has come in the hadith; and then [to set out] the discourse upon each name according to its rank, after alerting [you] to the secret of the enumeration (iḥṣāʾ). So I say — and in God is help sought: al-Tirmidhī related from Abū Hurayra — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((Truly God has ninety-nine names; whoever enumerates them enters the Garden. And they are these names: He is God, there is no god but He; al-Raḥmān (the All-Merciful), al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate), al-Malik (the King), al-Quddūs (the All-Holy), al-Salām (the Peace), al-Muʾmin (the Granter of Security), al-Muhaymin (the Overseer), al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty), al-Jabbār (the Compeller), al-Mutakabbir (the Supremely Great), al-Khāliq (the Creator), al-Bāriʾ (the Maker), al-Muṣawwir (the Shaper), al-Ghaffār (the All-Forgiving), al-Qahhār (the All-Subduing), al-Wahhāb (the Bestower), al-Razzāq (the Provider), al-Fattāḥ (the Opener), al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), al-Qābiḍ (the Constrictor), al-Bāsiṭ (the Expander), al-Khāfiḍ (the Abaser), al-Rāfiʿ (the Raiser), al-Muʿizz (the Giver of might), al-Mudhill (the Giver of abasement), al-Samīʿ (the All-Hearing), al-Baṣīr (the All-Seeing), al-Ḥakam (the Judge), al-ʿAdl (the Just), al-Laṭīf (the Subtle), al-Khabīr (the All-Aware), al-Ḥalīm (the Forbearing), al-ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent), al-Ghafūr (the Forgiving), al-Shakūr (the Most Thankful), al-ʿAlī (the Exalted), al-Kabīr (the Great), al-Ḥafīẓ (the Preserver), al-Muqīt (the Nourisher), al-Ḥasīb (the Bringer to Account), al-Jalīl (the Majestic), al-Karīm (the Generous), al-Raqīb (the Watcher), al-Muḥyī (the Giver of Life), al-Mumīt (the Bringer of Death), al-Ḥayy (the Living), al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), al-Wājid (the Finder), al-Mājid (the Glorious), al-Wāḥid (the One), al-Aḥad (the

Unique), al-Fard (the Sole), al-Ṣamad (the Eternal Refuge), al-Qādir (the Powerful), al-Mutaqaddir (the Determiner of measures), al-Muqaddim (the Advancer), al-Muʾakhkhir (the Deferrer), al-Awwal (the First), /fol. 127r./ al-Mujīb (the Answerer), al-Wāsiʿ (the All-Embracing), al-Ḥakīm (the Wise), al-Wadūd (the Loving), al-Majīd (the All-Glorious), al-Bāʿith (the Raiser of the dead), al-Shahīd (the Witness), al-Ḥaqq (the Real), al-Wakīl (the Trustee), al-Qawī (the Strong), al-Matīn (the Firm), al-Walī (the Protecting Friend), al-Ḥamīd (the Praiseworthy), al-Muḥṣī (the Reckoner), al-Mubdiʾ (the Initiator), al-Muʿīd (the Restorer), al-Ākhir (the Last), al-Ẓāhir (the Manifest), al-Bāṭin (the Hidden), al-Wālī (the Governor), al-Mutaʿāl (the Most Exalted), al-Barr (the Benign), al-Tawwāb (the Ever-Relenting), al-Muntaqim (the Avenger), al-ʿAfū (the Pardoner), al-Raʾūf (the Ever-Gentle), Mālik al-Mulk (Master of all Dominion), Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour), al-Muqsiṭ (the Equitable), al-Jāmiʿ (the Gatherer), al-Ghanī (the Self-Sufficient), al-Mughnī (the Enricher), al-Māniʿ (the Withholder), al-Ḍārr (the Bringer of Harm), al-Nāfiʿ (the Bringer of Benefit), al-Nūr (the Light), al-Hādī (the Guide), al-Badīʿ (the Wondrous Originator), al-Bāqī (the Abiding), al-Wārith (the Inheritor), al-Rashīd (the Rightly Guiding), al-Ṣabūr (the Patient).)) And these are ninety-nine names, which the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — enumerated out of the whole of the names of God, exalted is He. And you have already learned that the names of God, exalted is He, are many, and that the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — singled these out for mention only because they are comprehensive, containing within them the meanings that are the degrees of the Gardens. For that reason he said: ((Whoever enumerates them enters the Garden.)) And the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — did not mention the name that completes the hundred only because it is proper to him — God bless him and grant him peace — since its meaning is al-wasīla (the Means of Access), which is a degree in the Garden that is not fitting for any one of the servants of God, exalted is He, but belongs to the most perfect of His servants, our master Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace.
And know that whoever enters the treasure-house and comes forth with the abasement of disappointment dies in the fires of regret; and if he seeks to return to it, his face is blotted out.
Verse
Let him weep over himself whose lifetime has been squandered, and who has of it neither portion nor share.

So O the regret of one who has been heedless in the daylight of his negligence, and held back from the company of those possessed of the lordly gnoses! His loss has become plain beside the gains of the worlds, and his name has been erased from the tablet of those brought near. May God grant us and you refuge from the abandonment of being driven away, and preserve us and you from the ignominy of estrangement. Truly He is bountiful, generous, self-disclosing, comely, compassionate, munificent, magnificent.
Faṣl 1: On His name, exalted is He, Huwa Allāh alladhī lā ilāha illā Huwa (He is God, there is no god but He)

And if you say: Why have you not counted the name al-Ilāh (the God)? I say: The Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — did not count it among these ninety-nine names; rather he brought it in within what he predicated of the name of God, exalted is He, by way of the affirmation of oneness. And for that reason he did not make the whole of His name Huwa an independent name within this number; rather he counted, in place of it, His words He is God, there is no god but He (Q 59:22) as a single name — and that for a secret which those possessed of inner sight know.

As for His name, exalted is He, Huwa (He): it is a pronoun of absence, and it is among the most proper of His names, exalted is He, since true absence belongs to Him alone, for the intellects do not conceive Him and the imaginations do not delimit Him. And it is the name of the Essence, considered in respect of the all-encompassing reach of its absence and of its absoluteness from all the restrictions and descriptions that entail determinations (taʿayyunāt). And it is the opening of the names and the mother of their Book; and it may occupy among them the rank that the alif occupies among the letters. And it is a name of majestic worth, and it is said that it is the Greatest Name. And whoever makes it his litany of remembrance, being a brother of divestment (tajrīd), 11 times — so that nothing other than it occurs to his heart —

God opens for him, at the last time, a door of unveiling according to the measure of his preparedness. And it is among the names of majestic worth /fol. 127v./ proper to the greatest of those devoted to God (al-mutaʾallihūn). And it has, of number, 11; and it is the fourth prime number, and this number is from what the hāʾ requires. For that reason it was the fifth odd number; and it is an essential number, since it is a sealed whole in which there is no cleaving apart. And as for the names of its letters, they point to His name Hādī (Guide) from one aspect, and to His name Wāḥid (One) from another. And as for its square, it is according to this form:
[Wafq: 3×3, cells as in the source; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 372]
Fig. 64

[The corresponding square of names: 3×3, cells as in the source — (Munjī, the Deliverer), (Khafī, the Hidden), (Ṣāḥib, the Companion),(Mubīn, the Manifest),(ʿAdl, the Just), (Wafī, the Faithful),(Wāf, the Fulfiller), (Munjadh), (Kahf, the Refuge)]
Fig. 65

And as for His name al-Ilāh (the God): it is of majestic worth. It has a three-by-three square, complete in respect of its even number; and it has a four-by-four square in respect of its odd number. And the starting-point of its threefold square (muthallath) is from the letter hāʾ. Whoever engraves this threefold square upon a ring of silver, with Saturn in its exaltation, all the spiritual beings obey him; and whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes one who is obeyed in the world. I say: and if one of the gnostics utters it, the spiritual beings answer him after seven [days], following a fast and a litany of remembrance, and they ask what he desires. And it has, of number, 37 in utterance (lafẓan) and 36 in figure (raqman); and it is among the names that gather [the secret of] the even and the odd. And it has 43 in meaning; and that is by reason of the wāw's being latent within the hāʾ. And as for its square, it is according to this form which follows, and opposite it the threefold square. So ponder that, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills.

[The four-by-four square (murabbaʿ) of al-Ilāh: 4 columns, cells as in the source. The first row gives the names of the letters —(hāʾ), (alif),(lām),(hamza); the two middle rows give the numbers; the last row gives the names (Mubīn, the Manifest),(Huwa Awwal, He is First),(Hād, Guide),(Mubīn)]
Fig. 66

[The threefold square (muthallath) of al-Ilāh: 3×3, cells as in the source, the values written in abjad letter-numerals — =, 16 =, 11 = 9,, 8 = ,15 =, 14 =, 10 == 13, the centre cell being written as the numeral 12; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 36, the number of Ilāh. This is the threefold square to be engraved upon the ring of silver.]
Fig. 67

And as for His name, exalted is He, Allāh: it is a name of majestic worth, and it is a name in which the Maker (al-Bāriʾ) stands alone; and its meaning is "the Lord" (al-sayyid); and it is the comprehensive Name. For that reason all the names are a description of it, while it is not a description of any of them. And whoever multiplies the remembrance of it — no one can bear to look upon his face, out of reverence for the awe he inspires. And whoever writes it, with the Sun in its exaltation, upon a noble body, burns thereby every rebellious satan. And if he keeps it with him on a day of severe cold and multiplies the remembrance of it, he feels no pain of cold at all. And if one afflicted with the phlegmatic fever wears it as a signet, it departs at once. /fol. 128r./ And whoever engraves its square upon a thin parchment, with the Sun in Leo, and carries it after making remembrance of it 317 times — he does not lay his hand upon water but that that water sinks away, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And that is on condition that he be a man of [spiritual] state with God, exalted is He. And whoever knows its worth is made independent by it of every thing, for it is the Greatest Name of God, by which, when He is called upon, He answers, and when He is asked by it, He gives. And hence its manifest powers point to that: Huwa Mujīb (He is Answerer). And it is the first of the manifesting names, the gatherer of their realities, and that which comprises their fine points and their subtle threads. And it has a square according to this form; and its elevation (rafʿa) is sixty-six. Understand that, and you will be rightly guided.
[Wafq: 3×3, cells as in the source; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 66, the number of Allāh]
Fig. 68
[Wafq: 5×5, cells as in the source; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 66, the number of Allāh]
Fig. 69

And whoever draws it in a fivefold wafq and carries it, nothing of [his] affairs shall be hard for him, and by it hardships are made easy. And this is its form. And it is the litany of remembrance of the great ones, distraught with love, among the masters of the spiritual retreats. And it is suitable for one whose name is Muḥammad, that he multiply the remembrance of it. You say: Allāh Allāh; then he passes over the measure of a word; then he returns and says likewise again — in accordance with his words, God bless him and grant him peace: ((God, God is my Lord; I associate nothing with Him.)) And likewise for one whose name is ʿAbd Allāh. And it has, of number, 67 in utterance and 66 in figure. And as for the names of its letters, they are 260, pointing to two majestic names, namely ʿAlī (Exalted) and ʿAlīm (All-Knowing). So ponder it.
Faṣl 2: On His name, exalted is He, al-Raḥmān (the All-Merciful)

This noble name has a square of five by five, which is set down by the secret of interpenetration (al-tadākhul), with Saturn in its exaltation. Its possessor does not cease to move about within the good pleasure of God, exalted is He; no one sees him but that he grows tender toward him, and the religious communities come to him one after another. Whoever places it in water and gives one afflicted with burning fever to drink of it — it departs from him on the instant. And whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, the servants [of God] look upon him with the eye of mercy. Its remembrance is suitable for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. And know that whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it is treated with gentle kindness in all his states. It is related from al-Khaḍir — peace be upon him — that he said: Whoever prays the afternoon prayer on the day of Friday, and faces the qibla, and says "O God, O All-

Merciful" (Yā Allāh, Yā Raḥmān) until the sun sets, shall ask God for nothing but that He gives him what he has asked. And it has, of number, 298; and it is an even-odd, deficient number: its aliquot parts are 153, which point to His name, exalted is He, Mubqī (the Perpetuator). This is with respect to its figure (raqm); but with respect to its utterance (lafẓ) it has, of number, 299, /fol. 128v./ and it is an odd, deficient number: its aliquot parts are 37, which point to His name al-Ilāh (the God). As for the names of its letters, they are 406, which point to two majestic names, namely Mubdiʿ (the Originator from nothing) and Fāṭir (the Originator). And as for its square, it is in this form:

[Wafq: 5×5, cells as in the source; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 299 — the number of Raḥmān written with its alif. The top row holds the five letters of the name, which read from right to left
(raḥmān).]
Fig. 70
Faṣl 3: On His name, exalted is He, al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate)

This name, majestic in worth, is set in a square of four by four by the secret of interpenetration; and whoever carries it is treated with gentle kindness in all his states. Whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes one whose invocation is answered, and it is a security against the assaults of time. The time befitting it is when the Moon is in its exaltation. It is also beneficial for all burning fevers. And there is written together with its wafq And We send down of the Qurʾān that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers (Q 17:82). Its remembrance is suitable for one whose name is Ibrāhīm, and it is proper that there be adjoined to it his purified name. And it has, of number, 258; and it is an even-odd, oblong, composite number: it is al-Laṭīf (the Subtle) doubled, al-Badīʿ (the Wondrous Originator) tripled, and al-Awwal (the First) sextupled. And it is an abundant number: its aliquot parts are 270, which point to His name al-Karīm (the Generous). And this name has a wafq swift in effect. And this is its form, and it is as you see. Understand, and you will be rightly guided.

[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 258 — the number of Raḥīm. The top row holds the four letters of the name, which read from right to left (raḥīm).]
Fig. 71
[Wafq: 3×3, cells as in the source; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is likewise 258.]
Fig. 72

As for the names of its letters, [they are] 313, which point to His name, exalted is He, Yā Baṣīr (O All-Seeing), with the yāʾ of address. So ponder it. And God, glorified and exalted, knows best. Know, [all of] you — may God grant me and you success unto obedience to Him — that as for al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm, these are noble litanies of remembrance for those in dire straits and a security for those who fear. And no one engraves them upon a signet-ring on the day of Friday, at the end of the day, but that he is treated with gentle kindness in all his affairs. So ponder it.
Faṣl 4: On His name, exalted is He, al-Malik (the King)

This name is suitable for kings, and for others in their presence. It has a square of three /fol. 129r./ by three, which is set down upon a sheet of gold; and there is placed together with it Say: O God, Master of sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will (Q 3:26), to the end of the verse. It is among the majestic secrets: he who carries it does not cease to be held in awe and magnified in the souls of kings. The remembrance of it is suitable for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Malik, and its square is among the greatest of squares in benefit. And this is its form:
[Wafq: 3×3, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 90, the number of Malik]
Fig. 73

The author of Taysīr al-maṭālib ("The Facilitating of the Objects of Request") said: And if its numerical threefold square (muthallath) is engraved upon a leaf of gold, with the Sun in its exaltation, and a bezel-stone of red ruby is set upon it, and it is placed in a ring, and a king carries it with him — then he will not stand before any tyrant but that God, exalted is He, grants him success; and none will be able to endure looking upon him, even were he among the most courageous of created beings. So know it and ponder it, for it was in the hand of Dhū l-Qarnayn, and Plato the Sage devised its arrangement for him; and the lions would flee from him, by the occult property of the arrangement and of the name. And this is the form of its arrangement, and it is as you see. And perhaps some of them have arranged it in this form, and it is as you see. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided.

[Wafq: 3×3, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the three letters standing upon the main diagonal are (mīm, 40),(lām, 30), and (kāf, 20) — the letters of Malik — and the constant is again 90]
Fig. 74
[Fig. 75 — the second arrangement of the square, as in the source; not reproduced in the text stream — ]

And it is a noble arrangement, so guard it well, for it is of the red sulphur (al-kibrīt al-aḥmar). And it has, of number, 90; and this is among the realities of the letters of worship. And it is among the names arrayed in accordance with the ranks of number, in descending order. And it is an even-odd, oblong, abundant number: its aliquot parts are 144, which point to His name al-Bāqī (the Abiding), reckoned with its article. As for the names of its letters, they are 262, which point to His name Mujīb al-daʿwa (the Answerer of the invocation). So ponder it.
And God opens the pure hearts of the righteous to the understanding of the radiant secrets.
Faṣl 5: On His name, exalted is He, al-Quddūs (the All-Holy)

This name is of mighty worth. Whoever multiplies the remembrance of it until a state from it comes to prevail over him — God takes away from him every blameworthy appetite. It is set within a numerical threefold square (muthallath) encompassed by a letter-square (murabbaʿ ḥarfī), when Jupiter is in its exaltation; and as for its bearer, God exchanges for him, in place of every blameworthy trait of character, a praiseworthy trait. He becomes beloved to created beings and honoured among them, and God looses tongues in praise of him. And the remembrance of it is suitable for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Quddūs, and likewise for one whose name is Isḥāq. /fol. 129v./ And it has, of number, 174 in utterance (lafẓan) and 170 in figure (raqman). So it is among the treasured secrets, and among the mighty names that are even-numbered from every aspect. And this, in respect of the uttered number, is an even-odd, oblong, composite, abundant number: its aliquot parts are 176, which point to His name, exalted is He, Mūsiʿ (the Enlarger). As for its number in figure, it too is abundant: its aliquot parts are 191, which point to His name, exalted is He, Mannān (the Bounteous). And as for the names of its letters, they are 341, which point to two noble names, namely Ilāh (God) and Raqīb (the Watcher). And as for its square, it is according to this figure — so ponder it, for it is among the treasured secrets — and it is as you see.

[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the topmost row carries the letters of Quddūs —(qāf, 100),(the doubled dāl, 8), (wāw, 6),(sīn, 60) — and the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 174]
Fig. 76

It is the "numerical threefold square (muthallath) encompassed by a letter-square" announced at the head of the faṣl: a 4×4 lattice of diamond cells carrying the letters of Quddūs — —, , , encompassing a 3×3 numerical square that sits in the interstices. Faṣl 6: On His name, exalted is He, al-Salām (the Peace)

This name is of mighty station. No one has carried it with him and then had God, exalted is He, show him what he detests; and whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is kept safe from all afflictions. And in the remembrance of it there are secrets for the people of beginnings and secrets for the people of endings. No fearful one has multiplied the remembrance of it but that he was granted security, nor any deficient one but that he was made complete. And it has a square of four by four, and it is a square of mighty worth; and this is the form of its arrangement.

[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the topmost row carries the letters of Salām —(sīn, 60),(lām, 30), (alif, 1),(mīm, 40) — and the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 131]
Fig. 78

And it has, of number, 131, and it is a prime number, which points to His name, exalted is He, Kāfil (the Guarantor). And as for the names of its letters, they are 392, which point to two noble names, namely Raḥmān (the All-Merciful) and ʿAzīz (the Mighty). And the remembrance of it is suitable for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Salām, and likewise for one whose name is Muḥammad. And know that if you pair the odd number of al-Salām with one, that name is the name of Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace. /fol. 130r./ And he is the heart of the world, just as the heart of the Qurʾān is none but Yā-Sīn, and the heart of Yā-Sīn is "Peace!" — a word from a Merciful Lord (Q 36:58). And it is a verse of mighty worth, and in it is the Greatest Name of God. And it has a figure of mighty worth, to which I have alluded in the book Kashf al-asrār al-rabbāniyya ("The Unveiling of the Lordly Secrets"); so let whoever desires to put it to operative deployment come to a knowledge of it, for it is among the treasured secrets. So ponder it. And God, exalted is He, speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.
Faṣl 7: On His name, exalted is He, al-Muʾmin (the Granter of Security)

This noble name: its occult property is the granting of security. Whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God preserves his tongue from lying. And it has a square of four by four, which is set down when Jupiter is in its exaltation; and its possessor does not cease to be accepted among all created beings, and God makes easy for him the affair of his religion and of his worldly life. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Muʾmin. And it has, of number, 136; and it is an even-even-and-odd number, [its number being] the number of al-Ḥakīm (the Wise) twice. And it is a deficient number: its aliquot parts are 134, which point to Ṣamad (the Eternal Refuge). And as for the names of its letters, they are 299, which point to His name, exalted is He, al-Raḥmān (the All-Merciful). And this is the form of its arrangement:
[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 136, the number given in the text for Muʾmin]
Fig. 79
Faṣl 8: On His name, exalted is He, al- Muhaymin (the Overseer), glorified is He

This name is among the majestic, all-comprehending names. Therefore, whoever perseveres in its remembrance until a state from it comes to prevail over him, his knowledge encompasses its essence, and the hidden part of its secrets, and what God has brought forth concerning Him in the atoms of his existence, of faith and of acknowledgement. And whoever engraves it in a square upon a signet ring, with the Moon in its exaltation, or Saturn, after remembering the name by its number — God makes him secure from the evil of the accursed Satan. And if he perseveres in its remembrance and is the possessor of a truthful state, God, exalted is He, discloses to him the hidden part of his [Satan's] guile and his whispering. And it is among the names of encompassment, and it is the king of the all-comprehending [names]; none can gauge its true measure save one to whom the realities of the names have been unveiled. And it has, of number, 145; and it is an odd, oblong number, since it arises from the multiplication of the inward of all the letters gathered together, while it is in the outward of all of them, even in the outward of itself — and hence encompassment holds true of it. And it is a deficient number: its aliquot parts are 35, which points to the return of the whole affair to Him, by reason of His encompassing of it. And thence [arises] the query-term hal ("whether"), by which one asks about the aspects, for the realization of witnessing. And as for the names of its letters, they are 303, which point to two majestic names, namely Aḥad (the Unique) and Fāṭir (the Originator).

It is related of one of the rightly-guided caliphs — and he was ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb, may God be pleased with him, and God knows best — that he was asked about its meaning, and he paused over the answer. /fol. 130v./ And behold, a Bedouin woman possessed of a portion of eloquence brought before him the case of her husband, and said: O Commander of the Faithful, truly my husband is a bondsman where my right is concerned, and there he is at the threshold (al-waṣīd), and I have over him a muhaymin (an overseer) — so have you any mind for a musayṭir (a controller)? And thereupon ʿUmar, and those who were with him, glossed it as al-shāhid (the witness).

And this name has a square of five by five, and it is among the hidden secrets; and the beginning in it is from five, by the secret of His words, exalted is He: Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād (Q 19:1), Ḥā-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf (Q 42:1–2). And it is a natural odd number, because of what the odd numbers require of production, which is the fruit sought and the end intended. And for this reason the odd numbers are the more receptive to the world of contraction (qabḍ) and of majesty (jalāl), and the even numbers to the world of expansion (basṭ) and of beauty (jamāl). Faṣl 9: On His name, exalted is He, al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty), glorified is He

This name is magnificent in worth. It has a square of four by four, save that it cannot be set down by the secret of interpenetration (tadākhul), because of the repetition of the zāy in it. Whoever engraves it while Mars is in its exaltation shall have might over the enemies of God, exalted is He; and likewise whoever multiplies the remembrance of it. And whoever dreads having recourse to one of the princes, and humbling himself before him in the seeking of a need, let him multiply the remembrance of it; for whenever he multiplies the remembrance of it, /fol. 131r./ God, exalted is He, makes that easy for him without his humbling himself before anyone. I say: whoever multiplies the remembrance of al-ʿAzīz attains might in his religion and in his worldly life; and whoever perseveres in its remembrance, God, exalted is He, makes him mighty after his lowliness and secure after his fear. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz; and whoever understands its secret, God adorns his inward with the secrets of might. Do you not see that it points to His name, exalted is He, Yā Jamīl (O Beautiful), with the yāʾ of address? It has, of number, 94; and it is an even-odd, oblong, deficient number: its aliquot parts are 50, which point to the letter (nūn), which is the pivot of every thing — of inward knowledge and of outward provision — such that every thing humbles itself and seeks that of which it has need. As for the names of its letters, they are 178, which point to two majestic names, namely Malik (the King) and Ḥakīm (the Wise). So ponder that. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. Faṣl 10: On His name, exalted is He, al-Jabbār (the Compeller), glorified is He

This dazzling name: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it looks upon no one but that an awe of him overcomes that man, and he cannot endure to look upon him. It has a square of four by four, which is set down by the secret of interpenetration, with Mars in its exaltation. He who carries it is held in awe by all people, and no one meets with him but that he is abased before him and forsakes his own will for his. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Jabbār, and likewise for one whose name is Mūsā. It has, of number, 208 in utterance (lafẓan) and 206 in figure (raqman). He said: For the abasing of the tyrants (jabābira): it descends upon their high stations, and then it climbs upon their beards. Faṣl 19: On His name, exalted is He, al-Fattāḥ (the Opener), glorified is He

This name, lofty in station, majestic in proof: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God opens for him a door unto that toward which his aim is set. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for the wayfarers at the beginning of their states, and for those who have arrived, at the ending of them. And it has a square of four by four, which is set down by the secret of interpenetration (tadākhul); and its bearer sets his purpose upon no affair but that God opens for him a door thereto. And know that whoever takes it as a litany (wird) is not to take it [also] as a litany of remembrance. And whoever is driven by necessity to some need — after he has prayed two rakʿas on the night of Friday, he recites in the first [rakʿa], after remembering the enduring righteous [words] (al-bāqiyāt al-ṣāliḥāt) seven times, and they are "Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but /fol. 134v./ God, and God is greatest, and there is no power and no strength save in God, the Exalted, the Mighty" — this being before the recitation of the Mother of the Qurʾān (the Fātiḥa) and after it as well. Then he bows and remembers them likewise; and when he rises, likewise; and when he prostrates, likewise; and when he rises from the prostration, he does as at the first [time]. And likewise in the second rakʿa. And he recites Sūrat Yā-Sīn in the two of them, and Sūrat al-Mulk. And when he gives the salutation, he makes remembrance of the name after his takbīr; and then he will not ask God, exalted is He, for anything but that He grants him to attain it and gives it to him. And it [the name] is from inaugural opening (al-iftitāḥ) — do you not see its uprightness? And this is the form of its square:

And this name is among the odd-numbered names, in utterance and in figure alike. It has, of number, 889 in utterance (lafẓan); and it is oblong, because it is from the multiplication of 7 by 127. Faṣl 20: On His name, exalted is He, al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing)

This name, majestic in worth, manifest in proof — whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, gives him to look upon the fine points of the sciences and the hidden aspects of their secrets. And whoever engraves it upon a plate of congealed quicksilver, with Mercury in its exaltation, God, exalted is He, causes him to speak with wisdom and teaches him the subtleties of the gnoses. And whoever sets it upon a plate of silver, with Jupiter in its exaltation, is granted understanding in the sciences of the sharīʿa. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is ʿĪsā, and likewise for one whose name is Sulṭān. As for its square, it is according to this figure. So understand, and you will be rightly guided; and it is as you see. And it is sometimes set as a threefold square (muthallath) according to this figure.

[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the topmost row carries the letters of ʿAlīm —(ʿayn, 70),(lām, 30), (yāʾ, 10),(mīm, 40) — and the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 150, the number of the name]
Fig. 98

[Wafq: 3×3, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the middle row carries (70), the two letterstogether (10 + 40 = 50), and (30); the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 150]

/fol. 135r./ And in it there is a wondrous secret for the masters of the vizierate. I say: and whoever understands its secret, the necks bow down before him, and all the worlds are led in submission to him, and his free disposal (taṣarruf) within existence is strengthened, and God preserves him from calamities and wards off from him what he dislikes. And whoever perseveres in its remembrance learns knowledge of what he did not know, and wisdom appears upon his tongue.

And this name has, of number, 150; and it is an even-odd, abundant number. Its aliquot parts are 222, which point to His name, exalted is He, Mālik al-Mulk (Master of all Dominion). And hence the learned are in truth the kings; nay, they are the ones who hold mastery over the kings in their very kingship. And this number is among those in which the secret of the yāʾ has appeared in the three ranks; and it was a cause, and a subduing word, and a fashioning and a shaping by stages (taṭwīr) — since nothing of these three is completed save through knowledge, and nothing necessitates it save from it. So ponder that.

And since the locus of manifestation of knowledge among the holy spirits is the Gabrielic Spirit (al-rūḥal-jibrāʾīliyya), it was singled out for the teaching of the prophets; and among the noblest of them was our Prophet Muḥammad, God bless him and grant him peace — for it was revealed to him: "Be humble." God, exalted is He, said: One of intense powers taught him — a possessor of firm vigour — and he stood upright (Q 53:5–6). And since the holy spirit of Jesus (al-rūḥal-qudsiyya al-ʿīsawiyya) is the trace of the Gabrielic in-breathing into Adam — peace be upon him — and since Jesus, peace be upon him, was the most knowing of the prophets in the fine points of the sciences and the subtleties of the wisdoms, and among the noblest of his sciences was the science of the letter, hence this name was with him. And this is the community of Jesus, on account of what the name [ʿĪsā] indicates: from the ʿayn, knowledge; and from the yāʾ, the subtlety of descent; and from the sīn, the comprehensive sums of detailed exposition; and from the alif, encompassment. And it [the name ʿĪsā] has, of number, 141; and that is the number of the name ʿĀlim (the Knower). And since he was one who knew the hidden aspects of things, and ʿAlīm is said of him —
pointing to that — his name is written with a yāʾ [ʿĪsā spelt,]so that its number became 150; and that is the name ʿAlīm. So ponder that. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.

As for the names of its letters, they are 302, which point to His name, exalted is He, Baṣīr (the All-Seeing). And since the world is a sign that makes manifest the object sought, connected to Him with a complete connection — and it may be said [that knowledge is] the attainment of an essence connected [to it] with a complete manifestation, and this is the meaning observed by him who said that it is the attainment of the form of the thing in the mind — the meaning of al-ʿAlīm, in every case, is: He to whom the essence of every thing is manifest with a complete manifestation, joined to the outward of every thing and its inward. And it is among those secrets in which intensification by means of the wāw is not fitting, because of what it contains of elevation, [reaching] to the furthest of ends and to the whole of existence. Rather, intensification in it is made by the determinations of one of two things: either by reduplication, so that one says ʿAllām, and it then indicates the multitude of things known; or by the yāʾ, so that it indicates the descent to the fine points and the apprehension of hidden things. And ʿAlīm is not said save of one who knows the fine points as he knows the momentous things, and who knows the hidden things as he knows the manifest things. And for that reason God, exalted is He, said: and above every possessor of knowledge there is one all-knowing (Q 12:76). So the possessor of knowledge is he who knows the universals of things,

/fol. 135v./ and the ʿalīm is he who knows their particulars; and the possessor of knowledge is he who knows the outward aspects of things, and the ʿalīm is he who knows their inward aspects; and the possessor of knowledge is he who knows the manifest aspects of things, and the ʿalīm is he who knows their hidden aspects. And the meaning of this yāʾ has been obscure to many of the rational thinkers, so that [such a one] has denied His knowledge, exalted is He, of particulars.

Tanbīh. He, glorified and exalted, said: and above every possessor of knowledge there is one all-knowing (Q 12:76). So it is known that the superiority of some of the learned over others is not by the multitude of things known; for had it been so, He, exalted is He, would have said, "and above every possessor of knowledge is an ʿallām". Rather it is by attaining to the fine points of the things known and the hidden aspects of their secrets. Yes: a multitude of things known, if it be joined with precision, has an effect upon superiority; and if not, then not. And this meaning is what is intended by His saying, exalted is He, to His prophet Moses — peace be upon him: ((Yes: a servant of Ours at the meeting of the two seas, called al-Khaḍir; he is more knowing than you.)) al-Khaḍir was not more knowing than Moses in the sense that he had more things known — and how could that be, when God, exalted is He, has said concerning Moses: And We wrote for him upon the Tablets, of every thing, an admonition and a detailed exposition of every thing (Q 7:145)? Rather what is meant by it is that he knows the inward aspects of the things he knows as he knows their outward aspects. And for that reason his place was the meeting of the two seas, which are the sea of the outward and the sea of the inward. And he [al-Khaḍir] himself conceded to Moses — the blessings and peace be upon him — that he [Moses] possessed a knowledge from the knowledge of God, exalted is He, which he [al-Khaḍir] himself did not know.

So let your striving, O you who come upon these words, be that you become an ʿallām. And this meaning is what God, glorified and exalted, commanded His prophet to seek, in His saying, exalted is He: And say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge (Q 20:114). So ponder these spiritual words, and the subtleties of the All-Merciful, and the bestowals of faith, and the luminous draughts, and you will win an abundant share of the sciences of the masters of allusion. And God knows best.
Faṣl 21: On His name, exalted is He, al-Qābiḍ (the Constrictor)

This name, of majestic worth — whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, majesty and awe come to prevail over him, and no one has the strength to sit in his company. And whoever sets it in a plate of lead, with Saturn in its exaltation, and makes remembrance of the name according to its number, and says: "O God, constrict upon So-and-so his heart and his inmost secret" — he is answered in it on the instant. But if he is a wrongdoer, it is likely that this will come back upon him. And this name is among the litanies of remembrance (adhkār) of ʿAzrāʾīl, and in it there is a secret pertaining to the seizing of the spirits. And it has a square of majestic worth, a mighty one; and this is the form of its arrangement, as you see. And the combining of its letter-square (murabbaʿ ḥarfī) with its numerical threefold square (muthallath) is in this form, as you see.

[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the top row holds four divine names in place of figures — Ḥasīb (the Bringer to Account, 80), Jamīl (the Beautiful, 83), Muḥīṭ (the All-Encompassing, 67), Jalīl (the Majestic, 73) — and the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 303.]

And know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in obedience to Him — that whenever you desire the seizing of someone's spirit, then take it as a perpetual litany of remembrance, and say the name of the one whose destruction you desire; and that will be acted upon in the shortest span. So understand that. He said: And do not imagine that there will appear to you the effect of that from the [first] time, nor of Alif-Lām-Mīm Tanzīl (Sūrat al-Sajda). When the one who performs the remembrance perseveres in the remembrance and carries it on for a temporal hour, some of his worlds concur with him in it; and when he perseveres longer than that, his worlds and their spiritual beings (rūḥāniyyāt) come forward, performing the remembrance along with him. And at that point he sees the traces of the receptivities in himself and in others, in proportion to his presence, his purity, and the rectitude of his resolve. And this name is, of number, 903; and it is a number that points to gathering, which is among the exigencies of constriction, and to darkness, which is among the exigencies of straitness. And it is an odd, oblong, deficient number. Its aliquot parts are 505, which point to His name Rāshid (the Rightly Guided). And from here, whoever has caught the scent of it has caught the scent that the closing of the hand upon wealth is a mark of right judgement (rushd) — even as that has likewise been understood from His words, exalted is He: And if you discern in them right judgement, then hand over to them their wealth (Q 4:6). And as for the names of its letters, they are 1100, which point to His name, exalted is He, Mughnī (the Enricher).

Those possessed of the secrets have said: The Qurʾān will be taken up when its letters are complete, and that is at the completion of 903 years; and there will remain of the thousand 97 years, in which the most exemplary pass away, and then the next most exemplary, until there is not known upon the face of the earth one who knows God, exalted is He. The masters of lights have said: When time reaches the number of this name, there will appear the signs that indicate the coming of the Hour. And the masters of inner discernment (arbāb al-iṭṭilāʿ) have said: What remains until the coming of the Hour is this measure of years, and that is the duration of the Islamic religious community — may God, exalted is He, make it endure as long as the heavens and the earth endure. And this is the form of the hidden figure in which the date (taʾrīkh) of the Islamic religious community is recorded.

Faṣl 22: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Bāsiṭ (the Expander)

This hidden name and treasured secret: no fearful man makes remembrance of it but he is granted security, nor any sorrowful man but he is gladdened. And whoever engraves it upon a signet-ring in the first hour of Friday — his joy and his gladness increase, his worry and his grief depart, and everyone who sees him loves him. And if one possessed of a truthful state is assiduous in the remembrance of it, God expands for him his provision, /fol. 136v./ outward and inward, and revives his heart with the spirit of knowledge. And this name is one of the litanies of remembrance (adhkār) of Isrāfīl — peace be upon him — and by it the secret of the giving of life is made manifest, just as by al-Qābiḍ (the

Constrictor) the secret of the giving of death was made manifest. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is Maḥmūd. And know — may God grant success to me and to you — that whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it, his spirit is made easeful and his provision is expanded for him, even though he be of straitened means. And if he perseveres in it until a state from it comes to prevail over him, his worlds adorn him, and the mighty receptivities are acted upon for him. And that is because it points to His name, exalted is He, Qarīb (the Near). And it has a square, swift in effect, magnificent in worth, which is set within a numerical threefold square (muthallath) encompassed by a letter-square (murabbaʿ ḥarfī). And this is the form of its square, as you see.
Fig. 104

And it has, of number, 72. The two points to causality, and the seventy points to the very entity of the thing and to its subsistence. And it is an even-even-and-odd number, abundant by reason of the sense of detailed division (tafṣīl) that is in it, which belongs to the constricting grasp (qabḍa) of the sīn. And for that reason its aliquot parts are 123, which point to the word al-amān (security); for whomever God expands, He grants him security, and whomever He constricts, He makes him afraid. Faṣl 25: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Muʿizz (the Giver of might)

This radiant name and dazzling secret: no abased man persists in the remembrance of it but that he is made mighty, nor any obscure man but that he is made manifest. And it is among the majestic names, for in it there is a strengthening of aspiration (himma) and an aid toward deliverance from the enveloping coverings of [one's] nature. And whoever engraves it in a square and carries it with him is held in awe by all people, and every obstinate tyrant and rebellious satan takes fright at him. And it is among the mightiest of the litanies of remembrance of the believers. And know that no abased man perseveres in it with remembrance but that he is made mighty, nor any weak of aspiration but that his spirit is strengthened and God, exalted is He, reinforces him with abiding power and towering might; and he is held in awe among all created beings, and every obstinate tyrant and rebellious satan takes fright at him. And it has, of number, 124; and it is an even-even-and-odd, deficient number. Its aliquot parts are 100, which point, from among the letters of encompassment, to the letter (qāf) — and it is a letter that indicates manifestation with power and encompassment — and, from among the noble names, to two majestic names, namely Malīk (Sovereign) and Munjiz (the Fulfiller). For none is able to bring the entities into manifestation save He who is Owner of every thing and its Sovereign, the Fulfiller, for the people of sainthood, of what He has promised them of manifestation and of the granting of might — even as He, exalted is He, has said: that He may make it manifest above all religion, though the associators be averse (Q 9:33). And as for the names of its letters, they are 238, which point to two majestic names, namely Ilāh (God) and Rabb (the Lord). And this is the form of its square:

Faṣl 26: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Mudhill (the Giver of abasement)

This name, majestic in station — whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God abases the tyrants before him, and abases before him whomever He wills, also. And it is fitting that remembrance of it be made by one whose riding-beast has proved refractory toward him, and by one toward whom any one of created beings has proved refractory. And whoever takes this name as a litany of remembrance (dhikr), after a fast of three days the last of which is Thursday, and holds back on the night of Friday from breaking the fast, and prays two rakʿas — he recites in the first the Fātiḥa and makes remembrance of this /fol. 137v./ name a hundred times; and when he prostrates, he does the like of that; and he does in the second rakʿa as he did in the first; and he gives the salutation, and after the salutation makes remembrance of the name a thousand times, and says: O al-Mudhill, abase for me So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] — then that one is abased before him, and does not oppose him in a single matter, nor for a single breath. And God knows best. And know that everyone who makes remembrance of it with purity of the moment and with the turning [to God] of the one who performs the conjuration (al-muʿazzim) — it gives what lies within its power; and the failure of requests [to be granted] goes together with the absence of sincerity in the turnings [to God].

Laṭīfa (a subtle point). When the people of inner sight beheld, with the hearing of their hearts, the (dhāl) of abasement (al-dhull) — its place being with the (lām) of kindness (al-luṭf) and of connection — they knew that there is no connection to Him save through abasement. So they made themselves equal with the dogs in eating from the dung-heaps, and that bore for them as fruit the might that has no cutting off and admits no removal. Thus they were delivered from the pit of abasement before other than God, when they knew with faith, and beheld with excellence (iḥsān), that there is none that abases save God, exalted is He.

And it has, of number, 800, and it is an even-even number terminating in the odd at [its] kernel, arising from the multiplication of an oblong by a square. And it is among the abundant numbers. Mughnī (the Enricher); and the yāʾ was omitted because of the descent (tanazzul) that is in it, since whoever descends to anyone, that one abases him. As for the names of its letters, they are 892, which point to two majestic names, namely Dhū l-Quwwa (Possessor of Strength) and Mājid (the Glorious). And this name, strong in proof, has a square of majestic worth and of many benefits, and this is its form:

Faṣl 27: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Samīʿ (the All-Hearing)

This name, mighty in station, is fit to be made an object of remembrance at the end of every supplication; for whoever multiplies the remembrance of it at the end of every supplication is answered. Faṣl 29: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Ḥakam (the Judge)

And this name, of majestic station — whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, his word takes effect; and it is suitable for rulers and governors; and it is among the treasured secrets. And it has, of number, 68; and it is an even-even-and-odd number, and it is among the deficient numbers. /fol. 138v./ Its aliquot parts are 58, which point to His name, exalted is He, Azalī (the Pre-eternal), and to His name Maḥbūb (the Beloved), by reason of the indicator that lies within it. The ḥāʾ has appeared in the utterance, and in the number of the whole and of the parts. As for the names of its letters, they have, of number, 200 from one aspect and 201 from another. The first number points to His name Munʿim (the Bestower of favours), and to His name Musallim (the Bestower of safety), and to His name Ṣadūq (the Ever-Truthful); and all of that was from what justice requires. And the second number points to His name ʿĀṣim (the Protector), and to His name Nāfiʿ (the Bringer of Benefit), and to His name Fāḍil (the Excellent); and these three names are the more manifest when considered against the first three. Faṣl 30: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-ʿAdl (the Just)

This glorious name and manifest secret: whoever invokes with it against a wrongdoer, he is seized on the spot. And when a ruler multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, inspires him with justice among his subjects. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Muʾmin. And it has, of number, 104. As for the four, it is an indication of permanence; and as for the hundred, it is an indication of encompassment. And every king who has dealt justly with his subjects — his kingship has endured and his kingdom has grown wide; and kingdoms have been straitened and dynasties cut short only through the abundance of injustice. And this number is among the numbers that are even, even-even-and-odd, abundant. Its aliquot parts are 106, which point to His name Munjī (the Deliverer) and to His name Wafī (the Fulfiller); for whoever has dealt justly has fulfilled toward his subjects what is incumbent upon him, and so has delivered himself from blame and his subjects from injustice. God, exalted is He, said: O David, We have indeed appointed you a vicegerent upon the earth, so judge between the people with truth, and do not follow caprice, for it would lead you astray from the path of God. Truly those who go astray from the path of God — theirs is a severe torment, because they forgot the Day of Reckoning.(Q 38:26) And this name has a square of majestic station and mighty proof, and this is its form:

Faṣl 31: On His name al-Laṭīf (the Subtle)

This name — extraordinary in station, wondrous in proof, of majestic worth, swift in answering — is suited for the dispelling of anguish in times of hardship. It serves as a litany of remembrance for the captive and the imprisoned, and for one upon whom illness has grown severe, and for one who is subdued beneath the sway of his own nature and the rulings of his habits; and whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, makes easy for him deliverance from that. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is Ṣāliḥ. And this name has, of number, 129; and it is an odd, oblong number: the three measures it by forty-three. And it is among the deficient numbers: its aliquot parts are 47, which point to His name al-Wālī (the Governor), by reason of what subtle kindness (luṭf) contains of uninterrupted succession (tawālī); and to His name Mubdiʾ (the Initiator), by reason of what it contains of return to the rule of the primordial nature (fiṭra). And hence the reckoning of the first [factor] is by three. And as for the names of its letters, they are 172, which point to His name Muqbil (the One who turns toward). So ponder that. And God speaks the truth, and
He guides to the way — and He guides to Himself whoever turns to Him in penitence (Q 42:13). And in it is a wondrous secret for the fulfilment [of needs].

And know — may God, exalted is He, grant success to me and to you — as for the name al-Laṭīf: how swift it is to dispel anguish in times of hardship! No other name is joined to it. There appears from its effects wonder upon wonder. No one who is pained by something in his soul or in his body makes remembrance of it but that God removes it from him in the course of the remembrance. And no one makes remembrance of it while there is in his soul some mighty matter but that that matter is represented to him in his imagining; then he sets himself to the remembrance while observing that condition, and he does not fail to witness it — how it is dispelled and melts away — and he does not rise from his place with anything of his dread remaining. And in that are wondrous secrets and majestic matters. And this noble name has a square of majestic worth, mighty in station. And this is the form of its square.

And whoever sets it in a square, with Mercury in its exaltation, has majestic matters disclosed to him. And it has, of number, 812; and it is an even-odd, abundant number. Its aliquot parts are 868, which point to two majestic names, and they are Khāliq (the Creator) and Wāsiʿ (the All-Embracing). Faṣl 33: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Ḥalīm (the Forbearing)

This name, mighty in station and manifest in proof — whoever makes remembrance of it in the presence of a tyrant at the time of his anger, his anger is stilled; and likewise the angry man at the time of his anger. And whoever sets it in a square, with the Moon in its exaltation, and keeps it by him — his character is made goodly, his soul is set at ease, people come to desire his companionship, and he is made secure from harms and from agitation when hardships descend. And it is among the majestic names: none can esteem its worth save the gnostics. He said: And whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it attains all that he desires of al-maʿqala [uncertain: perhaps 'self-restraint', taking the ʿ-q-l root with this section's theme of forbearance; or a form of maʿqil, 'stronghold, refuge']. So understand that. And it has, of number, 88; and it is an even, even-even-and-odd number, and it is among the abundant numbers. And its aliquot parts are 92, which point to His name Amān (Security). And this name is among the most particular of the names of Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace. And for that reason he was a safeguard (amana) for his companions in this world and the next, and a safeguard for his people in this world; and for that reason his supplication was ((O God, guide my people, for they do not know)). And for that reason the number of his name, in figure (raqman), points to this name. And as for the names of its letters, they are taken according to the two reckonings: 183, which points to His name al-Mubqī (the Perpetuator), with the al-; and according to the second reckoning, 181, which points to His name al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), with the al-, and to Muʾallif (the Reconciler) without it. So understand that. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. And it has a square of majestic worth, and this is its form.

Faṣl 34: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent)

This is the red sulphur (al-kibrīt al-aḥmar) and the greatest magnet. Whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it, God grants him abiding might, and he is magnified in the eyes of the people, and his faults are veiled from them. And if he is one possessed of a truthful spiritual state and of complete directedness, he beholds the command of God, exalted is He, filling the engendered beings; he witnesses the command in every created thing. And God, glorified and exalted is He, knows best. /fol. 140r./ Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, grants him abiding might, and everyone who sees him loves him, and he is magnified in the eyes of the people. requires of magnitude (ʿiẓam). And its aliquot parts are 1096, which exceed the original. (wāw, ʿayn, ghayn): for the wāw is for elevation, to the all-comprehending gatherings of the bounty of existence; the ʿayn is an indication of manifestation, and the ghayn an indication of being veiled. Glory be to Him who is hidden by the very intensity of His manifestation! So the ʿayn and the ghayn: it is the name Ghanī (the Self-Sufficient). And it was the light of the light; and the yāʾ descends — it is its manifestation, the ghayn. Faṣl 36: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Shakūr (the Most Thankful)

Faṣl 37: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-ʿAlī (the Exalted)

This most great name and most illustrious secret — whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God ennobles his face, [keeping it] from abasement before any other than Him, and everyone who sees him loves him. And if he is one possessed of a truthful spiritual state, God, exalted is He, aids him with His help, and God, exalted is He, causes him to speak with wisdom and teaches him the subtleties of the sciences. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is ʿAlī. And God, glorified and exalted is He, knows best.

And know that one of the masters — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — said: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, raises high his worth and raises high his renown, and everyone who sees him loves him, and whoever is hostile to him is led in submission to him; and he sees in his lifetime radiant elevation, and in himself dazzling loftiness. And in it is a wondrous secret for the masters and the great ones, and for the seekers of the lofty sciences and the sublime affairs. And when it is joined to His name al-ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent), it is among the mightiest of the litanies of remembrance and the most majestic of them, and the noblest of secrets and the most perfect of them.

And know that whoever sets the two of them as a wafq upon a signet-ring of gold, and suffumigates it with aloeswood and ambergris, and carries it with him — then whoever sees him is abased before him and submits. And the kings used to adopt it, from al-Saffāḥdown to this time of ours — I mean the one in which he lived — so that their kingship is made firm and their power is spread wide. And it was said to al-Maʾmūn: "How will it be with you when the kings of Persia come upon you?" So he put forth his hand, with a signet-ring upon which were two names set as a wafq, and said: "No one shall have power over us so long as this remains engraved among us." And this is its form. /fol. 141r./ And the time befitting it is exaltation (sharaf).

Faṣl 39: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Ḥafīẓ (the Preserver)

This name, wondrous in station and evident in proof — whoever multiplies the remembrance of it upon a journey /fol. 141v./, God, exalted is He, preserves him until his returning from it. And whoever sets it upon a plate of silver, with Jupiter in its exaltation — it is not laid upon anything but that it preserves it from everything from which harm is feared for it. And whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is preserved in all things. And know: as for His name al-Ḥafīẓ, it is swift of response for the fearful upon journeys. He does not cease to make remembrance of it in the places of fears, and God does not show him what he abhors. And indeed it was imparted to me in the places of plunder and seizure, and I threw myself upon the remembrance of it, and I saw of the wonders of God's making what no one can grasp. And whoever engraves it upon the bezel of a signet-ring of silver — its number as a wafq — and its permutation (taksīr) as letters upon the inner side of the signet-ring, and carries it: were he to sleep in the beast-haunted places of the earth, nothing he abhors would reach him. And he adds after it: Yā Ḥafīẓ (O Preserver), preserve me. I say: as for its permutation (taksīr), it is according to this form; and as for its wafq, it is according to this form.

I say: and whoever fears that he may fall into a matter he has no strength for, let him multiply the remembrance of it; and he who is on his guard against something he fears cannot dispense with carrying it. So understand that, and ponder. And it has come by a sound channel of transmission: whoever recites the Throne Verse (Q 2:255) before his going out from his house, nothing befalls him until he returns. Al-Kirmānī said: and if he gives in alms something of his wealth to the poor and the needy before his going out from his house — the least of that being to seven needy persons — it is a cause of safety upon the road. So ponder that. And God is the One who makes [things] light, and who grants success in that wherein is His good pleasure.

A company passed by a man sleeping beside a thicket, with his mare grazing at his head; and he was stirred, and it was said to him: Do you not fear to sleep in this place, when it is a haunt of beasts of prey? So he raised his head and said: I am ashamed before Him that I should fear any other than Him.

And whoever realizes himself in this name of majestic worth — God, exalted is He, preserves for him his times, his stillnesses, and his purest states; as is related of Abū ʿAlī b. al-Daqqāq — may God be pleased with him — that he said: One of the righteous inherited ten thousand dirhams, and he said: My God, I am in need of these dirhams, but I do not know how to keep them well, so I hand them over to You, that You may return them to me at the time of my need of them. So he gave them in alms to the poor and the needy, and he cleaved to [spiritual] poverty (faqr); and that man never had need of anything for the whole length of his life — whenever he had need of something, it was opened to him. So understand.

Faṣl 41: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Ḥasīb (the Bringer to Account)

This name — majestic and radiant, exalted and dazzling — whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is sufficed in his upkeep, his need is fulfilled, his invocation is answered; and he asks God, exalted is He, for no matter but that He grants it to him, because in it is an indication of the Greatest Name of God. And it has, of number, 80; so it is among the simple names. By "the simple" I mean those that revert, in number, to a single letter, as this name reverts to the letter (fāʾ). For the root of al-Ḥasīb is nothing other than gathering and encompassing; so it requires the mastering of the things scattered abroad by grasping the aspects under which they are found. And it was expressed by the fāʾ only because reckoning (ḥasb) is a dividing limit between two parties settling accounts, and by it contention is cut off; for reckoning is a dividing limit between those who dispute. And likewise too, if it be taken in the sense of al-Kāfī (the Sufficient): for sufficiency is a dividing limit between the one who is sufficed and everyone other than the Sufficient. And it is among the abundant numbers: its aliquot parts are 106, which point to His name Munjī (the Deliverer), by reason of what the sense of sufficiency requires of deliverance — that is, from need of another — and by reason of what the sense of enumeration (iḥṣāʾ) requires of indulgence after it, as God, exalted is He, has said: Then God delivers those who were godfearing, by reason of their place of triumph /fol. 143r./(Q 39:61). And how excellent is he who said:
They called us to account and were exacting; then they granted favour and set [us] free.
Such is the mark of kings: with those they own they deal gently.
Truly my heart says to me, and my tongue speaks true:
Everyone who dies a Muslim is not burned in the Fire.

And it points also to His name, exalted is He, Musabbib (the Causer); for whoever calls you to account has thereby set up a cause, either for the manifesting of his bounty or for the manifesting of his justice. And for this reason the bāʾ, which entails causation, was brought in at the end of the name al-Ḥasīb, and its ending was unto a causation from which bounty or justice becomes manifest. And it points also to His name, exalted is He, Wafī (the Fulfiller); for whoever calls you to account has thereby fulfilled toward you what you claim from him — all the more so when he knows what is with you of deficiency or of excess before the reckoning. And reckoning, among things counted, stands as weighing does among things weighed; and so it stands in need of al-Wafī, which stands over against short measure (taṭfīf). And if we take al-Ḥasīb in the sense of al-Kāfī, then al-Musabbib and al-Wafī are manifest within it. And as for the names of its letters, they are, by one of the two considerations, 143, which point to His name al-Mubīn (the Evident), by reason of what reckoning contains of making clear (tabyīn), and to His name al-Musaddid (the One who directs aright), with the al-; for the two of them are so by reason of what reckoning likewise contains of that. And this number is by the odd of al-Kāfī (the Sufficient) and, by its even, al-Mujmil (the One who sums up), by reason of what the leaving-off of reckoning contains of summary comprehension (ijmāl). And as for the other consideration, they are 146, which point to the word by which everyone is sufficed in his needs, namely Allāhumma (O God), and to that which is preferred above it, which is ḥasbiya Llāh (God is my sufficiency). This is in respect of what the sense of sufficiency requires. And as for what the sense of numbering requires, it points to this same phrase, which is equity (ʿadl), by reason of what numbering contains of that. So ponder what I have pointed out in this
— section. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.
Faṣl 42: On His name, exalted is He, al-Jalīl (the Majestic)

This noble, hidden name and subtle, treasured litany of remembrance — whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes great in the inner sights of hearts, and everyone who sees him holds him in awe. And whoever engraves it at the time befitting it and carries it with him subdues thereby every obstinate tyrant; and its action upon what is absent from you is like the action of al-Kabīr (the Great) upon what is manifest to you. So take heed of what I have pointed out to you. And God bestows His bounty upon whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of mighty bounty. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Jalīl. The master Zayn al-Dīn al-Khāfī [base text: al-Ḥāfī] — may God sanctify his spirit — said: In this name there is a majestic secret for those who seek awe (hayba) and majesty. And whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, no one is able to look upon him, out of reverence for him; nor does the gaze of any tyrant fall upon him but that he is filled with dread of him at the sight of him, so that it is as though the secret of majesty were upon his heart for as long as the gazing upon him lasts. And it is suitable /fol. 143v./ for warriors on campaign and for the commanders of armies. So understand that.

And it has, of number, 73; and it is a prime number. For the meaning of al-Jalīl, by reason of its all-comprehensiveness and its subtlety, is a closing-up in which there is no rending open. And the (jīm) appeared in it to indicate gathering (jamʿ), and the (ʿayn) is an indication of manifestation (ẓuhūr); and al-Jalīl gathers up the meaning of al-Jāmiʿ (the Gatherer) together with al-ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent). And for that reason the names of its letters exceed the things they name by this number, 134. Or it points to His name, exalted is He, Ṣamad (the Eternal Refuge), and to His name Mufīd (the Bestower of benefit), and to His name al-Munjī (the Deliverer), with the al-. For al-Jalīl is He to whom recourse is had in every matter, that He may bestow every good and deliver from every evil. ((Cleave persistently to "O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-
Ikrām" (Possessor of Majesty and Honour).)) And as for its square, it is according to this form, as you see.

Faṣl 43: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Karīm (the Generous)

And when al-Wahhāb (the Bestower) and Dhū l-Ṭawl (Possessor of Bounty) are joined to it, it is among the wonders. And know: as for His name, exalted is He, al-Karīm, and al-Wahhāb, and

Dhū l-Ṭawl — none whose provision has been straitened and whom destitution has touched persists in these litanies of remembrance but that God, exalted is He, makes things easy for him from whence he does not perceive. And whoever engraves these names and hangs them upon himself does not know how God makes the objects of request easy for him without hardship. And measure by analogy against it whatever accords with it of states, of words, and of acts. I say: and these noble names have a square swift in effect and lofty in station. And this is its form.

And it is fit as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Karīm. And it has, of number, 270; and it is an even-odd, abundant number. And it has a square of majestic worth and mighty in station, and this is its form, and it is as you see. So understand that.

Faṣl 44: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Raqīb (the Watcher)

This greatest name and most generous secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is preserved in his movements and in his stillnesses, and in all his states and his acts of free disposal. Faṣl 45: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Mujīb (the Answerer)

This most luminous name and greatest secret is fit for the answering of invocations; and it ought to be adjoined to all the names whenever a request is intended by them. And whoever engraves it in a square on Friday, while the preacher is upon the pulpit, and then perseveres in the remembrance of it until the setting of the sun — he asks God, exalted is He, for nothing but that He gives it to him. And it has, of number, 55; and it is an odd, deficient number. Faṣl 46: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Wāsiʿ (the All-Embracing)

This noble name and subtle secret: whoever makes remembrance of it, God enlarges his provision, his character, and his knowledge, and grants him deferment in his appointed term. And it is among the names of majestic worth, for whoever knows its worth. And he who carries it does not come to be in any straitness but that he finds from it an amplitude; and God appoints for him, out of every affair, a relief and a way out. The master Zayn al-Dīn al-Khāfī [base text: al-Ḥāfī] — may God, exalted is He, have mercy on him — said: Whoever perseveres in the remembrance of this all-comprehending, radiant name and lofty, dazzling secret — God enlarges his provision, makes goodly his character, spreads out his inmost secret, and expands his breast. And it is among the majestic names, for whoever knows its worth. And whoever sets it down in broken form (kasr) in a four-by-four square, with the Moon in its increase, and makes remembrance of it after the recitation of the Fātiḥa, and carries it with him — God makes easy for him difficult matters, and enlarges for him provisions and means. And in it is a wondrous secret in relation to kings, princes, grandees, and viziers. And there is no king who multiplies the remembrance of it but that his kingdom becomes wide and his word goes forth. So understand that. And it has, of number, /fol. 145r./ 137. The seven is for deliverance from straitness; the thirty is for the ordering of all the names within the amplitude of its bond; and the hundred is for its encompassment and its manifestation. And for that reason this number was all-comprehending of the first of the names in manifestation and of the lowest of them in descent, which is in reality the last of them in manifestation; and that is Ilāh (God), Malīk (Sovereign). And this number, if the like of it be reckoned upon it by the jummal, that yields wāsiʿ qalbuhu ("capacious is his heart"); and if the like of it be reckoned upon it, that yields qalbuhu wāsiʿ ("his heart is capacious"). And the allusion therein is to Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — since he is the believing servant alluded to in His saying, exalted is He: ((The heart of My believing servant has embraced Me)). And this number is among the prime numbers. And it was so only because the outward sense of the expression, inasmuch as it entailed being a receptacle (ẓarfiyya) for every thing — such that its manifestation stands as a barrier before the manifestation of every thing — the closing-up (al-ratq) was therefore more deserving of this meaning than the rending open (al-fatq). This, withal that He, exalted is He, is hallowed above indwelling in anything, or anything's indwelling in Him. These are but noble allusions, understood by subtle tastings.

*A fine point (nukta). Whoever witnesses the Magnificence says: I have seen nothing but that I saw God, exalted is He, after it. And whoever witnesses the Amplitude says: I have seen nothing but that I saw God, exalted is He, before it. For the eye (al-ʿayn), which is the inward of the Magnificence, is the outward of the Amplitude. And for that reason the Magnificence was a waist-wrapper (izār). So ponder that, for it is among the subtleties of divine oneness (tawḥīd*).

And as for the names of its letters, they are the number 374, which point to the sphere of the Spirit, by reason of the amplitude of its encompassment. God the Magnificent said: on the day the Spirit and the angels rise up, rank upon rank (Q 78:38). And this is the form of the disposition of its square.
