Faṣl 47: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Ḥakīm (the Wise)

This splendid, dazzling name and sublime, radiant, glorious secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, inspires him with wisdom concerning the fine points of the sciences, and casts to him the marvels of the meanings and the subtleties of the allusions. And it is among the names of majestic worth. And whoever sets it down in the first [hour] of Wednesday, with Mercury in its exaltation, upon a body befitting it, and carries it with him, making remembrance of the name, having assimilated the character (takhalluq) of the sages and being schooled in their comportment — the divine effusion is redoubled upon him, and the wellsprings of wisdom burst forth from his heart upon his tongue. And the operation with it is conditioned upon the purification of the soul. God, exalted is He, said: God has indeed shown favour to the believers when He raised up among them a messenger from among themselves, reciting to them His verses, and purifying them, and teaching them /fol. 145v./ the Book and wisdom (Q 3:164). And God, exalted is He, said: He it is who raised up among the unlettered a messenger from among them, reciting to them His verses, and purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom (Q 62:2). And the master Zayn al-Dīn al-Khāfī [base text: al-ʿĀfī] — may God, exalted is He, have mercy on him — said: Whoever multiplies the remembrance of this noble name and subtle litany of remembrance, God, exalted is He, gives him to look upon the secrets of wisdom, and teaches him the fine points of the gnoses, and inspires him with the subtleties of the meanings, and gives him to understand the realities of the secrets of the oft-repeated [verses] (al-mathānī). And it is among the treasured secrets and the hidden traces. And whoever sets it down upon a plate of congealed quicksilver, with Mercury in its exaltation, is granted understanding in the sciences of wisdom. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for the sages. And in it is a wondrous secret for the vizierate. And this is the form of its square, as you see. Understand, and you will be rightly guided.

Laṭīfa (a subtle point). The wise man sees straitness as amplitude, while he against whom judgement is passed by the decree sees amplitude as straitness. Faṣl 48: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Wadūd (the Loving)

This attracting magnet and procuring ruby: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes beloved in the sight of everyone; and God makes the hearts of created beings firm upon love of him, and makes his own heart firm. And it is among the beautiful litanies of remembrance. And whoever sets down His name Wadūd and His name, exalted is He, Ḥasīb (the Bringer to Account) in a threefold square (muthallath) whose centre /fol. 146r./ is with Jupiter in a conjunction of love, and carries it with him, is granted the love of hearts. And whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it and in the remembrance of the name al-Dāʾim (the Everlasting), his blessing endures. And it is fitting, in that the figure is, in [the matter of] love, of majestic worth. And know that whoever writes this name upon a white silk cloth thirty-five times, with the moon in its house and in conjunction, let him set it down in the first [hour] of Friday, with Venus in its exaltation; then let him persist in the remembrance of these names, and he will see marvels. And the operations of this are munificent (jawād). And [as for] the setting of the threefold square within the interior of a square of 96 — no one's gaze falls upon him but he loves him. And whoever wishes to set down this figure of magnificent worth, let his carrying of it be in a state of purity and fasting. And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see.

And some have set it down in this following form, and it is a litany of remembrance noble in its setting-down, so guard it well. And some of the masters have mentioned that whoever multiplies the remembrance of it until a [spiritual] state from it comes to prevail over him — then whoever sees him inclines to him by his very nature and loves him in his inmost being; and God, exalted is He, gives life to his heart and his inward by the spirit of love, and adorns his outward with the secrets of affection. So ponder that and you will be rightly guided. And this is the form of what is promised by its remembrance, as you see.
Fig. 137

And whoever sets it down in a four-by-four square by the names of its letters, in the first [hour] of Friday, and persists in the remembrance of it until the setting of the sun — no one's gaze falls [upon him] but he loves him. And in it is a strange secret and a wondrous meaning, for the attracting of the inward parts and the spirits and the procuring of the outward parts and the bodily forms. And it is a litany of remembrance for the masters of beauty, and for him who has tasted of the drinking-place of love and has sat upon the carpet of affection.
Fig. 138

Do you not see that its letters correspond to Badūḥ, and that the names of its letters point to His name Sūl (the Object of Request), and the aliquot parts of its number to His name Ḥabīb (the Beloved)? So understand. And as for its majestic wafq, of lofty renown, this is its form, as you see. Understand, and you will be rightly guided. So ponder that and you will be rightly guided, if God — glorified and exalted is He — wills. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.
Fig. 139

And this noble name has, of number, 20; and it is an even-even-and-odd number. There corresponds to it among the names Hādī (the Guide); and it is among the noble numbers. ((Show affection to one another and you will love one another.)) And as for the names of its letters, they are

96, which point to His name, exalted is He, Sūl (the Object of Request); for the Beloved, the Loving, is Himself the object of request. And when it produces its effect, there is affection — for it comes from the multiplication of the first cube number by the first number behind it. And it is an abundant number, its aliquot parts being 22, which point to His name Ḥabīb (the Beloved); for love is the fruit of affection. Love — from it is made the pursuit, which is among the traces of His name, exalted is He, Ṭālib (the Pursuer). So reflect upon that; and God bestows His bounty upon whom He wills, and God is All-Embracing, All-Knowing. And if you say: What is love? we say: the purity of affection. And it has been said: the perpetual inclination, with a heart distraught with longing. Faṣl 49: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Majīd (the All-Glorious)

And whoever multiplies the remembrance of it until a [spiritual] state from it comes to prevail over him — his word is not turned back. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Majīd. And it has a threefold square (muthallath) of majestic worth; and this is the form of its arrangement:

Faṣl 50: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Bāʿith (the Raiser of the dead)

This most great name and most luminous secret is suitable for one whose resolve has grown weak in some matter; and whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is roused up to every good. Some of them said: it serves for the prevailing of life and health over the bodies, and for the preservation of the powers. If you desire that, then take clean garments, and fumigate with aloeswood and clove, and recite the name in a spiritual retreat (khalwa) made ready, and in purity of heart, until a [spiritual] state from it accrues to you; for God supplies you with strength and rouses your aspiration to the acts of obedience. The master Zayn al-Dīn al-Khāfī [base text: al-Kāfī] — may God, exalted is He, sanctify his inmost secret — said: Whoever engraves this majestic name and beautiful secret upon a plate of lead in the first [hour] of Saturday, then makes remembrance of the name 4011 times while he gazes upon its drawn figure with a gaze of majesty, and then says: "O Zuḥal (Saturn), I have set you in power, by such-and-such, over So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]" — that comes to pass swiftly, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted is He. And this is the form of its square, and it is as you see:

And it has, of number, 573. The ʿayn and the thāʾ in it remain as they are, while the bāʾ of causation was taken together with the upright alif — which is the Causer of causes — so that there appeared the jīm, which indicates conjunction and the union of the cause with the Causer. And this number is odd and deficient. Its aliquot parts are 195, which point to His name, exalted is He, Ṣādiq (the Truthful), and to Mawlā l-mawālī (the Master of masters). And God, glorified and exalted is He, knows best.
Faṣl 51: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Shahīd (the Witness)

This lofty name and sublime secret: whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it, it yields him watchful vigilance (murāqaba) in his spiritual retreat (khalwa) and in his coming forth into company (jalwa). And if he is a possessor of a state of assimilation of character (takhalluq), that yields him the dyeing of his soul with the dye of unity and justice, so that he is secure from excess and from defect in the whole of /fol. 147v./ his soul's traits of character. And it is among the majestic litanies of remembrance. Some of them said: it is suitable for one who seeks the rank of martyrdom (shahāda). And I did indeed command one of the jurists to make remembrance of it, and he attained that at once. And the author of ʿIlm al-hudā mentioned that whoever inscribes it in the first [hour] of Friday upon a sheet of paper, to the number of its outward powers, before the Possessor of Lights (Dhū l-Anwār), and hangs it upon his heart without any barrier, the bodily forms bear witness to his generosity and his excellence, and mouths [base text: al-aqwāh] speak for him of his right guidance and his intellect; and God provides him with gravity, awe, might, and splendour. And it is among the treasured secrets. And it has a square of majestic worth, mighty in station. And this is the form of its arrangement:

And this name has, of number, 319; and it is a prime number, because its meaning, by reason of the threat it comprises, is a closure with no rift in it: Say: God suffices as a witness between me and you (Q 17:96). And as for the names of its letters — 412 — they point to His name, exalted is He, Mujrī l-fulk (the Setter of the ship in motion), because the ship courses before the eye of God, exalted is He, so He is its witness, even as there has come concerning that His word, exalted is He: coursing before Our eyes (Q 54:14). So understand that, and you will be rightly guided.
Faṣl 52: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Ḥaqq (the Real)

This name, mighty in station and lofty in proof: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, makes him firm in the acts of obedience, and makes manifest through it the realities of things, and gives him to look upon the hidden things of the secrets, and makes falsehood hateful to him, and makes his word subduing and exalted. And it is among the names of magnificent worth; and by it God makes firm those who believe. And whoever engraves its square under the ascendant of one of the fixed signs (al-burūj al-thawābit), upon an instrument in which he wishes to make firm something that has no firmness — God makes it firm for him. And that comes about only after the remembrance of the name, until a [spiritual] state from it comes to prevail over the one who makes remembrance. And there is written upon the surface of the square, on its four sides: But as for what brings benefit to people, it abides in the earth (Q 13:17). And this is its form:

[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; four of the sixteen cells carry words instead of figures —(Awwal), (Ilāh),(Muḥīṭ) and (Kāfī) — and the wholly numerical rows and columns sum to 208, the number of the name in utterance]

And as for the second number, it is an even-even-and-odd, abundant number; its aliquot parts are 172, which point /fol. 148r./ to His name Muqbil (the One who turns toward). So understand that. And this is the form of its square:

Faṣl 53: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Wakīl (the Trustee)

This radiant ruby and dazzling secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, suffices him, and makes him independent of secondary causes, and provides for him whence he does not reckon. And if he be a possessor of a truthful state, he eats from the world of being (al-kawn). And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is Muḥammad. And it has a square of majestic worth; and this is its form:

And whoever gathers its numerical wafq and its letter wafq in a single square — [it is] upon this form, as you see.
Fig. 147

And it has, of number, 66; and it is an even-odd, oblong number. And this name is among the names that belong exclusively to Muḥammad and to the family of Muḥammad; and for that reason God, exalted is He, named him in the earlier scriptures al-Mutawakkil (the one who puts his trust [in God]). And by reason of the comprehensiveness of this name it has a special relation to the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace. It corresponds in number to the all-comprehending Name: for Allāh is 66, and Wakīl is 66, and the sum of that is 132, and that is his name — God bless him and grant him peace. And this number is an abundant number, according to what has preceded; its aliquot parts are 78, which point to His name Ḥakīm (the Wise), for if the trustee (wakīl) is not wise, he does not set things in their [proper] places. And concerning that, verse has been spoken:
When you send a man upon an errand, send one who is wise, and give him no instructions.

And the aliquot parts of each of the two names exceed its own base by 12; and that is His name, exalted is He, Aḥabb (Most Beloved), and it is among the names most proper to him — God bless him and grant him peace. And when the excess of the one is joined to the other, that comes to /fol. 148v./ 24, which is his name — God bless him and grant him peace — and His beloved. So the sum of the names is Muḥammad and His beloved, just as the sum of each of the two was Allāh [and] ḥubb (love), or Wakīl [and] ḥubb. And as for the names of its letters, they are 197, which point to His name, exalted is He, al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), with the article — by reason of what trusteeship (wakāla) contains of standing over [affairs] (qiyām).
Faṣl 54: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Qawī (the Strong)

This name, magnificent in worth: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is strengthened by it for the carrying of heavy burdens, outward and inward; and his spirit is strengthened, and by it he gains command over everything. And it is among the litanies of remembrance of ʿAzrāʾīl. And it is fitting that one who labours at the carrying of heavy burdens should engrave it and carry it. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is Mūsā (Moses); and it is proper that His name al-Mubdiʿ (the Originator from nothing) be added to it. And likewise for one whose name is Yūnus (Jonah). And know that whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it does not grow weary in his journey, so long as he persists in its remembrance and in the carrying of it. And as for its square, it is according to this form:
[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 126, the number of the name in utterance (lafẓan)]
Fig. 148

And it has, of number, 126; and it is an even-odd, abundant number. Its aliquot parts are 186, which point to a majestic litany of remembrance — whoever cleaves to it, nothing shall render him powerless — and it is Allāh maʿī (God is with me). This is what its numbers give you to understand, in utterance (lafẓan). But if you consider it in figure (raqman), it is 116; and it is an even, even-odd, deficient number; [its aliquot parts are] 94, which point to His name, exalted is He, ʿAzīz (the Mighty). And for that reason might (ʿizza) is the companion of strength (quwwa). And the first number points to Mūsā, and the second points to Yūnus. And as for the names of its letters, they are 206, which point to His name, exalted is He, Jabbār (the Compeller); and it is the place of manifestation of Mūsā. By [another] reckoning, 218, which point to His name, exalted is He, Muṣfiḥ (the One who overlooks [faults]); and it is the place of manifestation of Yūnus — peace be upon him. And know that whoever is nearer to the Presence of His name al-Qawī, and whose witnessing of it is the more complete, is the more bound to weakness, by reason of the turning to the Real (al-Ḥaqq) from the standpoint of that name. For that reason Mūsā — peace be upon him — said: And my brother Hārūn is more eloquent than I in tongue, so send him with me as a support; truly I fear that they will deny me (Q 28:34); Truly I have killed a soul among them, and I fear that they will kill me (Q 28:33); So Mūsā conceived within himself a fear (Q 20:67); They both said: Our Lord, truly we fear that he may act rashly against us, or that he may transgress (Q 20:45). The Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said ((concerning Yūnus b. Mattā, peace be upon him: He was a weak man)). And look at how the two of them share in being cast into the sea /fol. 149r./ — this one in the darkness of the chest (al-tābūt), and that one in the darkness of the belly of the whale. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills.
Faṣl 55: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Matīn (the Firm)

This name of majestic worth: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it does not grow weak before a matter he has strength for, even were it doubled. And it is fitting that whoever fears the cutting off of his strength in some matter or other should multiply the remembrance of it. And when it is adjoined to al-Qawī (the Strong), it is of the utmost swiftness of efficacious influence in respect of one who labours at the carrying of heavy burdens. And know that whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it until a [spiritual] state from it comes to prevail over him becomes awe-inspiring, possessed of strength, valour, leadership, and might. And in it is a wondrous meaning for the subjugation of kings. And it has, of number, 500; and it is an even-even-and-odd, abundant number. Its aliquot parts are 592, which exceed the original by that to which His name Amān (Security) points. For in firmness (matāna) there is security from the derangement of strength; and for that reason its end is the nūn, which is the existence of that through which manifestation and the making-manifest come to be. God the Magnificent said: Truly the best of those you might hire is the strong, the trustworthy (Q 28:26). And God, mighty and majestic is He, said: Truly We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they refused to bear it and were afraid of it; and man bore it (Q 33:72). And they refused to bear it and were afraid of it only because they, though they have strength, have no firmness; and firmness is the trust (al-amāna) — that is, the security against the cutting off of strength. Then He said: and man bore it; truly he was a great wrongdoer— to himself, by laying upon it what it has no strength to bear — exceedingly ignorantof the cutting off of his strength, for want of his trustworthiness. And as for the names of its letters, they are 608, which point to two majestic names, namely Mukrim (the Honourer) and Rāziq (the Provider). And this is the form of its arrangement:

Fig. 149
Faṣl 56: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Walī (the Protecting Friend)

This sublime, dazzling name and radiant secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God takes him under His protection and takes him as His friend. And it is among the litanies of remembrance of the angels of the exalted Presence, those who are called the cherubim (al-karūbiyyūn). Whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it, realizing its meaning — which is the removal of the intermediaries — is established in the station of sainthood (wilāya). And know that the one who makes remembrance of it: nothing of the states of created beings calls upon him but that he is given an unveiling of it. And it has, of number, 56 in utterance (lafẓan) and 46 in figure (raqman). As for the first number, it is an even-even-and-odd, abundant number; its aliquot parts are 60, which point to His name, exalted is He, Mubīḥ (the One who makes lawful) — because whoever has removed the intermediaries between himself and God, exalted is He, has had made lawful to him, from Himself, what is forbidden to others. And as for the second number, it is an even-odd, deficient number; its aliquot parts are 26, which point to a

/fol. 149v./ majestic name that is among the litanies of remembrance of the greatest of those who profess [His] oneness, namely your saying Aḥad Aḥad (Unique, Unique). For the walī (the saint) is he whose parts and particulars speak forth this litany of remembrance. And as for the names of its letters, they are 96, which point to His name, exalted is He, al-Dayyān (the Requiter), with the al- — so understand. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is Muḥammad. And this is the form of its arrangement:

Faṣl 57: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Ḥamīd (the Praiseworthy)

This lofty litany of remembrance and manifest secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes praiseworthy in his qualities, thanked for his deeds, and magnified in the eyes of all people. And whoever writes it by its number in a cup (jām) and gives it to drink to one who has an illness, God, exalted is He, heals him of it. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is Maḥmūd. And know that whoever realizes this name is praiseworthy in character; and whoever unveils it with a complete unveiling is the most praiseworthy of you. And as for Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — he is the locus of manifestation of praise, His manifest creation; and he is the opening of the Book of Existence, as he said — God bless him and grant him peace: ((The first thing God, exalted is He, created was my light.)) For he — God bless him and grant him peace — is entirely praise. With him the Real, exalted is He, opened the Book of Existence, for it is a matter of consequence; and had He not begun it with the praise of God — who is Muḥammad and the most praiseworthy of them — it would have been maimed. And for that reason the last call of the prophets was his call, by force of And the last of their call is: Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds (Q 10:10). So he — God bless him and grant him peace — is the Opener and the Seal, just as he is the Praise. And just as the Real — glorified, exalted and hallowed is He — opened with him the Book of the Beginning, so likewise God, exalted is He, will open with him the Book of the Return, as he said — God bless him: ((I am the first over whom the earth will split open.)) And for that reason he — God bless him and grant him peace — was singled out with Sūrat al-Ḥamd, which is the Fātiḥa of the Book, His mighty Book, from a treasure beneath the Throne that was not opened save by his name —

God bless him and grant him peace — Aḥmad. So understand these luminous tastings and ṣamadānī secrets, and you will win an ample portion of the knowledge of the bestowals of faith and the gnoses of the heart. And God — glorified and exalted is He — speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.

And this name has, of number, 62; and it is an even-odd, abundant number. Its aliquot parts are 34, and they point to your saying Huwa Ṭabīb (He is a Physician). And as for the names of its letters, they are 147, which point to your saying Huwa Muʾmin (He is a Granter of Security); and by another reckoning it is Muhaymin (the Overseer), or al-Jāmiʿ (the Gatherer). And as for its square, it is according to this form. So understand, and you will be rightly guided, if God — glorified and exalted is He — wills. And praise be to God alone, and God bless … … … /fol. 150r./ And this is the form of its square, as you see.
[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 62, the number of the name]

Faṣl 58: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Muḥṣī (the Reckoner)

This name, majestic in station and magnificent in proof: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, gives him to inherit watchful vigilance (murāqaba). And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one for whom al-Ḥasīb (the Bringer to Account) is suitable — except that, this [name] being free of the bāʾ, it is less in threat and in affliction. And it has, of number, 148. So the eight is for perfection, and the forty for completeness, and the hundred for encompassment; and al-Muḥṣī is He who possesses a perfection that is complete and all-encompassing. And this number is an even-even-and-odd, deficient number. Its aliquot parts are 118, which point to His name, exalted is He, Muḥṣī (the Reckoner) among the people of the secrets, and to Ḥayy Malīk (Living Sovereign) [readingfor the edition's ] among the people of the lights; and that is by reason of what life requires of perfection, and kingship of encompassment.

Tanbīh. Know, all of you — may God, exalted is He, grant you success — that the generality of what has preceded, from His name al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate) to His name al-Ḥamīd (the Praiseworthy): the notice they give (iʿlāmuhā) is only in respect of what pertains to the meaning of the secondary causes (asbāb) — such as al-Wahhāb (the Bestower), al-Karīm (the Generous), al-Razzāq (the Provider) and their like — and to knowledge — such as al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), al-Samīʿ (the All-Hearing), al-Baṣīr (the All-Seeing), al-Ḥakīm (the Wise) and their like — and their conclusion has come to be al-Ḥamd (praise). But as for what is ranged in order along with them, from the name al-Muḥṣī to His name al-Ṣabūr (the Patient), the generality of them lie in a rank that brings into being the servant's incapacity, as has appeared in al-Muḥṣī, and as will appear in al-Mubdiʾ (the Initiator) and al-Muʿīd (the

Restorer) and the rest, if God, exalted is He, wills, up to al-Ṣabūr; and in [a rank] that brings gnosis into being as a disposition, as has appeared to you in His name al-Hādī (the Guide). And it is as though He, glorified and exalted is He, began with that in which creatures have the semblance of a share — even if only by [their own] claim — and then sealed with that in which they have no share at all; rather all of them confess their incapacity before it, such as the initiating [of creation], and the restoring, and the giving of life, and the giving of death. So ponder that. And God knows best. And as for the names of its letters, they are 205, which point to two majestic names, and they are ʿAzīz (the Mighty) and Kāfī (the Sufficient). And this is the form of its square, as you see.

Faṣl 59: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Mubdiʾ (the Initiator)

This luminous name and lordly secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, the hidden aspects of affairs are disclosed to him, and God, exalted is He, causes him to speak with wisdom; and nothing of him becomes apparent to anyone save what he wishes. And it is among the majestic names, for whoever desires the accomplishment of his affair in the world of generation. And whoever /fol. 150v./ perseveres in it, his works become good and endure. And it is suitable for whoever wishes to make a beginning in some affair among affairs. And know — may God grant me and you success — that whoever is assiduous in the remembrance of it grows intimate with the sublime sciences, and speaks of the matters of wisdom, and speaks in verse. And it has, of number, 56. So it stands to al-Walī (the Protecting Friend) as al-Wakīl (the Trustee) stands to His name, exalted is He, Allāh. And therefore, when the two are joined together, His name, exalted is He, Mubīn (the Evident), appears; and by patronage (walāya) and initiation — which is the bringing to manifestation — everything is made evident. And as for the names of its letters, they are 141, which point to His name, glorified and exalted is He, ʿĀlim (the Knower). And as for its noble square, this is the form of its arrangement, as you see.

Faṣl 60: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Muʿīd (the Restorer)

This noble, spiritual name and verdant, all-merciful name: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it sets right by it everything corrupt, and recovers everything that has gone. And when it is set down with one of the movable signs (al-burūj al-munqaliba) in the ascendant [reading

for the edition's ,]and is hung up in the path of the wind, and the person keeps on reciting the Name the whole night long over a runaway slave or a traveller, he returns to his place from which he went out, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted is He. And for that reason the Real, glorified and exalted is He, manifests Himself by the name al-Malik (the King), since it is the day of restoration. And this number also indicates the letter (qāf), by reason of what lies in the encompassment of the utmost limit of the descent of the beginning (al-badʾ). And as for the names of its letters, they are 266, which point to two majestic names, namely Malīk (the Sovereign) and Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting). Faṣl 61: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Muḥyī (the Giver of Life)

This dazzling name of self-sufficiency (ṣamadānī) and radiant lordly secret — whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, gives him life by the spirit of divine oneness (tawḥīd), and gives life through it to every thing. And it is among the litanies of remembrance of Isrāfīl. And know that whoever perseveres in this name, God, exalted is He, gives life to his heart and makes manifest the power of his inward in his outward; and in it there is a relation (nisba) to /fol. 151r./ His name al-Ḥayy (the Living). And whoever engraves it upon a signet-ring of steel at the time of the Friday prayer and wears it, God, exalted is He, gives life to his heart and to his renown, and magnifies his worth, and he sees of the subtlety of God, exalted is He, toward him what descriptions are powerless to encompass. And it has a square of majestic worth, which the masters of the secrets know. And it has, of number, 68; and it is an even-even-and-odd, deficient number. Its aliquot parts are 58, which point to His name, exalted is He, Azalī (the Pre-eternal). And as for the names of its letters, they are 144, which point to His name, exalted is He, Muʿizz (the Giver of might), by reason of what there is in giving life of the granting of might, and in bringing death of abasement. And this is the form of its square.
[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 68, the number of the name]

Faṣl 62: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Mumīt (the Bringer of Death)

This name, mighty in station and evident in proof, is for whoever intends by it the destruction of the wrongdoers and the cutting off of the last remnant of the transgressors. And no one multiplies the remembrance of it and then invokes against a wrongdoer but that he perishes on the spot. And it has a mighty efficacious influence (taʾthīr) in quieting what is stirred up of appetite. And no one perseveres in the remembrance of it until a [spiritual] state from it comes to prevail over him, and then makes mention of the name of the one whose destruction he intends, but that God, exalted is He, destroys him on the spot. And it has, of number, 490; and it is an even-odd, abundant number. Its aliquot parts are 536; and it is a number which niʿma l-mawlā (excellent Patron) measures by twos. Faṣl 72: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Muʾakhkhir (the Deferrer)

This luminous, majestic name and beautiful, all-merciful secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it has a subduing operative deployment (taṣrīf) in the world. And whoever operates by it as has preceded in the foregoing [name], it gives him what lies within its power. And it ought not to be made a remembrance except together with al-Muqaddim. And know that whoever wishes to advance someone to his [proper] rank, let him depict a form upon a tablet after the most beautiful of forms, and let him set the tablet before him, gazing at it with gathered aspiration, purity of the inward, and presence of heart, while he makes remembrance saying Yā Mutaqaddim (O Foremost), until a [spiritual] state from it comes to prevail over him. And he may behold the form performing the remembrance along with him; let him not flee, but keep to that state for a temporal hour, for his need will be fulfilled by the leave of God, exalted is He — especially for the masters of [spiritual] states. So understand that, for it is not possible to declare more openly than this saying in this place. And God knows best. And this is appended to the secret of His name, exalted is He, Muqaddim (the Advancer). So understand, and measure what is absent by what is present, and the circle of understanding will widen for you. And be a believer in it, even if there is not opened to you a door from the Dominion (malakūt) through which the secrets are witnessed. So glory be to Him who has granted the gnostics the enjoyment of the unveiling of the secrets of self-sufficiency (ṣamadāniyya), and has barred the doubters from the well-spring of the substance of the lordly lights.

And this name has, of number, 1446 in utterance (lafẓan) and 846 in figure (raqman). And it has a square of majestic worth, which the masters of inner sight (baṣāʾir) know. So ponder it, for it is among the treasured secrets.

Faṣl 73: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Awwal (the First)

This healing, noble name and lofty, subtle secret: whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it becomes one who presses onward to the virtues, by the leave of God, exalted is He. Faṣl 74: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Ākhir (the Last)

This noble name and subtle secret: whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it will be the one who remains after his enemies, and God, exalted is He, will give him the earth to inherit after them; and none will show him enmity but that God, exalted is He, destroys him. And know that whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it — God gives him of strength against the enemies, and of victory over them, what tongues are powerless to describe; and he has awe-inspiring presence and acceptance. And whoever writes it upon a tablet of red copper in the first [hour] of the day of Saturday, with the moon in the dark of the month (muḥāq) — or [where the writing] proceeds from perfect faith and a collected inmost being — while he recites the Name until he perceives its efficacious influence (taʾthīr) according to his state, and then casts it into the fire: that wrongdoer, against whom the operation has been performed in his name, perishes after a few days, according to what certain of the scholars — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them — have expressly stated concerning that. And this name has, of number, 802; and it is an even-odd, deficient number. Its aliquot parts are 404, which point to two majestic names, and they are Rabb (the Lord) and Munʿim (the Bestower of favours). And it has a noble square, of majestic worth, known to whoever has inner discernment (iṭṭilāʿ) of the occult properties (khawāṣṣ) of the names and the secrets of the numbers. And this is its form.

Faṣl 75: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Ẓāhir (the Manifest)

This name of exalted worth and secret of manifest affair: whoever persists in the remembrance of it, the Real, exalted is He, makes manifest to him the hidden aspects of affairs, and by it treasures are brought forth. And it has a square of majestic worth, which the people of the lights know by its congruity [reading for the edition's .] Some of them have said: whoever engraves it upon a sword and fights with it will be the one who triumphs and prevails over his enemy — especially if he be a possessor of a truthful state. And it has, of number, 1106; and it is /fol. 157r./ an even-odd, deficient number, its aliquot parts being 814, which point to two majestic names, namely Jāmiʿ (the Gatherer) and Khafī (the Concealed). And as for the names of its letters, 1222, they point to two majestic names, namely Mughnī (the Enricher) and Maʿbūd (the Worshipped). And it has a noble square, which the masters of inner discernment (arbāb al-iṭṭilāʿ) know; and this is the form of its arrangement:

Know that as for His name, exalted is He, al-Nūr (the Light), and al-Bāsiṭ (the Expander), and al-Ẓāhir (the Manifest) — it is the litany of remembrance of the masters of the unveilings. And whoever wishes to behold something in his sleep, let him make remembrance of these names in a state of purity while he is in his bed, until he falls asleep upon this litany of remembrance, and let him set his aspiration (himma) to work upon what he desires; for the unveiling of that will be represented to him in his sleep. And God, glorified and exalted is He, knows best.
Fig. 175
Faṣl 76: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Bāṭin (the Hidden)

This mighty, lordly name and generous, self-sufficient secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is made safe from what he fears, and his soul is set at rest, and his heart is enlarged, and his inward is illumined. And some of them have said: whoever persists in the remembrance of it until its worlds accompany him and make remembrance along with him — he comes to no land but that its people turn to him with kindness and obedience, and with him are all the worlds; and everyone who sees him loves him, and everyone whom he calls answers his invocation with kindness. And in it are secrets for the people of divine oneness (tawḥīd) which none know but they. And whoever gathers together within a square its numerical and its letter secrets — of the letters and of their names — is given to look upon the inward aspects of the secrets and their realities. And it is among the noble litanies of remembrance for one who has a spiritual discipline (riyāḍa). So take to the remembrance of it with its conditions. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is Muḥammad.

The master Zayn al-Dīn al-Khāfī [base text: al-Kāfī] — may God sanctify his inmost secret — said: Whoever writes it by its number, with the moon increasing in light, in a bowl of glass, and multiplies the remembrance of it until a state from it comes to prevail over him, and effaces it with rainwater and drinks it for a number of days equal to its number, while he is seeking the lordly unveilings and the luminous gnoses — he attains them; and nothing of the affairs of the world remains hidden from him but that God, exalted is He, gives him to look upon it in his sleep, or in his waking [reading for the edition's

,] according to his state. And if he be a possessor of a truthful state and of complete orientation, the veil of the husk is lifted from his inward, so that he needs no explanation along with it; rather that is a plain, verified unveiling and a sound, well-guided description. So understand the symbol, and conceal the treasure, and make your belief sound — you will prosper. And God has, within every one of the names, wisdoms and secrets and subtleties and effects such as are not grasped by the way of rational speculation, but rather by something beyond that, which he grasps who has been dislodged from halting with the intelligibles to what lies beyond that, of noble secrets and wondrous effects. And above every possessor of knowledge there is one all-knowing (Q 12:76).

And know — may God bring you forth from the abysses of the dense things to the degrees of the subtle things — that just as He alone is the One characterized by manifestation, so He alone is the One characterized by hiddenness; and His is the hiddenness to whose ending there is no limit. So it comes about that every hidden thing is a manifest thing in relation to what is /fol. 157v./ more hidden than it. So the Command is the hidden aspect of creation, and He to whom belong the Command and creation is hidden from them both; and so the hiddenness of the Command is a matter of relative consideration, not a real one, and the Hidden in reality is none but He such that, when a coursing [ray] from His light courses forth, it makes manifest every hidden thing.

And this name has, of number, 62; and it is an even-odd, deficient number, its aliquot parts being 34, which point to this noble phrase, namely your saying huwa Ṭabīb (He is a Physician). And as for the names of its letters, they point to the inward of the human being, which is his heart, since their number is 132. So they are written as heart after heart: [the heart] of the Qurʾān, which is expressed by Yā-Sīn, and [they point] to the heart of the world, which is expressed by Muḥammad — in the tasting (dhawq) of some, and to both matters in the tasting of certain others. And His name al-Bāṭin is the origin of unity and of justice, and the heart is the locus of the manifestation of them both. And Muḥammad the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — is the most hidden of what has become manifest to creation, and the most manifest of what has been hidden of the Command. And in another respect they point to His name al-Munīl (the Bestower) and al-Sanī (the Sublime). And as for its wafq, it is mighty; and this is the form of its arrangement, as you see. So understand, and you will be rightly guided.

And this name has, of number, 551; and it is an odd, deficient number. And if the wind grows distressful, or turns against the people of a ship, and they multiply the remembrance of it, the fair wind comes to them. And know — may God, exalted is He, grant success to me and to you — that whoever drinks much wine and commits much fornication, and makes remembrance of the name seven hundred times every day, comes to loathe all of that. And it has, of number, 402 in utterance (lafẓan) and 202 in figure (raqman). As for the first number, it is an even-odd number, which al-Nāfiʿ (the Bringer of Benefit), al-ʿĀṣim (the Protector), and al-Munjī (the Deliverer) — with the article — and al-Mufīd (the Bestower of benefit) without it, measure by threes; and it is among the abundant numbers. This name, mighty in worth, the lofty; magnificent in proof, the manifest: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, makes easy for him the return to his origin. Faṣl 82: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-ʿAfuww (the Pardoner)

This shining name and gleaming secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, there are made beloved to him the noble traits of character and the refraining from taking [others] to task for sin. Faṣl 83: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Raʾūf (the Ever-Gentle)

Faṣl 85: On His name, exalted is He, Dhū l- Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour)

This majestic, magnificent, luminous name, and wise, lordly litany of remembrance, is among the majestic names. And it has come [in tradition] that it is the Greatest Name of God; and for that reason, whoever multiplies the remembrance of it does not ask God, exalted is He, for anything without His granting it to him. And in the hadith: ((Cleave persistently to "O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām")). And whoever writes it upon a chest in the first [hour] of the day of Thursday — it is preserved from thieves and robbers, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And whoever looks upon its drawn figure and its inscribed secret every day, by the number of its letters, while he recites the name — God makes easy for him the affairs of this world and the next, according to what some of the masters — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — have laid down. And this name has, of number, 1100; and it is an even-even-and-odd, abundant number. And the Proof of Islam, Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī — may God be pleased with him — mentioned in Iḥyāʾ ʿulūm al-dīn ("The Revival of the Religious Sciences") that whoever makes remembrance and says after the Friday prayer: "O God, O al-Ghanī (the Self-Sufficient), O al-Ḥamīd (the Praiseworthy), O al-Mubdiʾ (the Initiator), O al-Muʿīd (the Restorer), O al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate), O al-Wadūd (the Loving): enrich me by what You have made lawful, so that I have no need of what You have forbidden; and by obedience to You, so that I have no need of disobedience to You; and by Your bounty, so that I have no need of any besides You" — whoever perseveres in this holy litany of remembrance, God, exalted is He, enriches him so that he has no need of His creation, and provides for him from whence he does not reckon. And he said: ((Whoever does not call upon God, He is angry with him)). And he said: ((Truly God loves those who are insistent in supplication)). And in another hadith: ((Truly God does not weary until you weary)).

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant you success in the understanding of the meanings of the vessels and in the unveiling of the secrets of the letters — that harm is according to the measure of knowledge and encompassment. And when the Real — exalted and hallowed is He — willed to stand alone in this name, He made the harm of every harmer a benefit for the one harmed, by what He appointed upon it of reward and recompense and of welfare immediate and deferred. For if a person had an enemy in whose humoural temperament the blood had come to predominate, until it was near to destroying his spirit, such that, were he to remain in his condition, he would die that very night — and [the other] hastened to harm him and struck him a blow that diminished his blood — then his harming him would be the utmost benefit for that harmed man, because of his ignorance of the seat of the harm. The Explanation and Occult Properties (khawāṣṣ) of the Junnetu'l-asmāʾ
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 324
Hujjetu'l-Islām Imam Ghazālī (may God be pleased with him) relates the following.

I was residing at the Nizamiye Madrasa in Baghdad, the city where the ascetics (ābidīn) and the Kutb and Ewtād — [saints of the highest spiritual ranks] — lie buried. I taught knowledge to students (tālib) as best I could, and at times gave sermons. One day, while I was sitting alone, there was a knock at the door; I opened it. A man entered, gave the greeting of peace, and said: "I come from the Commander of the Faithful, His Excellency the Caliph. The Caliph wishes to see you at once." I said, "Could we not go an hour from now?" He replied: "By no means! His Excellency the Caliph requests that you come immediately." "Very well, let us go. Bismillah!" — saying this, I rose from my place and mounted a donkey.

When we arrived at the palace, I saw that they were waiting for me. They took me to a private room; the Caliph entered and greeted me with honor. In response I stood up. The Caliph said to me: "O Imam, my purpose in summoning you so urgently is this: in the palace treasury I found several documents written on leather, left behind by my ancestor Hārūn er-Reshīd. These were written by the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali (may God ennoble his countenance); they are extremely difficult to read, and no one has been able to read them or discover what is written in them. While I was still a child, the Caliph before me would, at the start of every year, place it upon his head with reverence and honor, open it, hold it in the smoke of fragrant incense (bakhūr) while praying, and pass it over his face and eyes. Then he would return it to its chest. He would take it with him into battles, and always won. I follow the same custom, but I am curious as to what is written in the documents. O Imam! In this age there is no scholar of religion greater than you. Be gracious and generous, and resolve this difficulty of mine." I said: "O Sultan! May God the Exalted gladden you in this world with every kind of favor and grace, and may your rank be exalted in the hereafter as well, for you honor the scholars. God willing, the Merciful, I shall fulfill this wish of yours." The Caliph gave an order to a young man; they opened the treasury and brought a chest adorned with every kind of jewel. The chest was opened, and inside it another chest, made of steel, was found. Its key hung on a chain attached to it. That steel chest, too, was opened, and inside were several documents wrapped in silk. The Caliph took the documents, passed them over his face and eyes, and then [I 325] handed them to me. I took the documents with reverence and respect, and opened them. I saw that, just as had been said, they were written in the blessed hand of Hazreti Ali (may God ennoble his countenance), in Kufic script. I examined them a little and began to read. It opened with the noble Basmala, praise and thanks to God Almighty, and then it spoke these couplets:
Men lam akwāluna terdeuh
(Whoever rejects our words, we too shall reject him wholeheartedly.)

After this couplet, two odes (qaṣīda) were written. In them were counsels concerning this world and the next, and certain divine names (asmāʾ). Through symbols (rumuz) he sought to convey the Greatest Name (Ism al-Aʿẓam) to those worthy of it, while concealing it from those who were not. Alongside these, also in Kufic script, he explained his purpose in writing these two odes and the manner in which he had composed them.

In them he says: a great plague broke out in Kufa and Basra. Many people died. Indeed, in some places the losses were so great that the dead could not be buried, and birds of prey began to devour the corpses. (I had read in the history books that a plague occurred in Kufa and Basra during the caliphate of Omer el-Fārūk, may God be pleased with him. Was this that same outbreak, or did it happen later? In any case—)

At a time when this disease had spread everywhere, Abdullah ibn Ebu'l-Munzir (may God be pleased with him), one of the notables of Kufa, rose and came to me. He spoke to me of the suffering and afflictions the Muslims were enduring, and asked how they might be delivered from it. I said: "O Ebu'l-Munzir! There are many prayers which the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, recited when such conditions occurred. Why do you not recite them and ask the Almighty to remove this disease?" Ebu'l-Munzir said: "By God, O Imam! After the five daily prayers we recite, as best we can, whatever prayers we know, and we implore. But we obtain no result." Hazreti Ali (may God ennoble his countenance) said:
("Truly we belong to God, and truly to Him we shall return.")

[I 326] "Is it, perhaps, that your prayer is not accepted, or that your intention is not sincere? Or is there mockery (istihza) in your prayers?" "God forbid, my lord, we do not mock in prayer. But, as you say, our intention is not sincere. Be gracious, and teach us that Greatest Name which you learned from our exalted Prophet, so that we may write it and carry it upon our heads." "O Ebu'l-Munzir! To say plainly what you ask would be to disclose (ifshā) the Greatest Name. But I will tell you a few things. This will be a means of delivering you from affliction and plague. If someone, out of ignorance, does not accept our words, then let this verse of God, glorious and exalted, [be recited against him]:
(Indeed, they devised their plots and schemes, and their schemes are known to God; even if their scheming were enough to move mountains, they shall be requited for it.)
Because of this, let ruin come upon that disbelieving denier. [Recite also] the 122nd noble verse of Sūrat el-En'ām:
He said that this noble verse

consists of 19 letters, that these letters are written on the foreheads of the guardians of Hell (zebānī), and that it is because of these letters that they are able to withstand the fire of Hell; and he named six (6) divine names whose letters likewise total nineteen (19). He explained that these names are sharper than a sword and repel the fire of the plague.

Hazreti Ali, may God ennoble his countenance, also gave Ebu'l-Munzir this counsel: "This method I have shown is a remedy for every spiritual illness and affliction. When you write this Junnetu'l-Asmāʾ (Shield of the Names), write it in a solitary place, and show what you have written to no one! Let your heart also hold good intention. You must be clean and in a state of ritual purity (abdest), and anoint yourself with pleasant fragrances. When you write it for someone and give it to him, tell him not to open and look at it, for it will have a greater effect that way. You must teach this only to people who are clean of face, virtuous, and righteous — [I 327] I grant permission (icazet), by the grace and leave of God, glorious and exalted, to whoever knows and carries these documents," he says.

Imam Ghazālī, may God be pleased with him, relates: after I read these writings and explained them to the Caliph, he was very pleased, and asked me to write down exactly what I had told him and give it to him. I agreed. The Caliph gave me a period of three days. I took the documents and went to my house. I studied them with a tranquil heart, wrote one copy for the Caliph and one for myself, and reported to His Excellency the Caliph. He gave me leave, and bestowed upon me every kind of favor and generosity.

Through these names I attained many divine favors. Even my bearing and appearance improved. One day someone said to me: "O Imam! We always used to see you as weak and sickly, but these days we see a different state in you. Your face is full of light and your body is healthy. What, I wonder, is the cause of this sudden change? Be so gracious as to tell us, so that we too may improve thanks to you." I answered that person's question appropriately, and cautioned him to conceal this secret from those unworthy of it. I myself occupied myself with these names on certain occasions.

I had gone somewhere as a guest. On my way back, we were attacked by bandits on the road. There were about a hundred (100) horsemen. They had charged at full gallop into our caravan. The people of the caravan with me were frightened; they had given up all hope for their goods and their lives, and stood trembling with their arms bound. I, this poor servant, uttered the Takbīr ten (10) times in the manner Hazreti Ali, may God ennoble his countenance, had taught, and recited the Asmāʾ al-Aʿẓam (the Greatest Names) toward them nineteen times. Suddenly the horses were startled and stopped where they stood; they could not take even a single step. One of the bandits called out to us: "O people of the caravan! For the sake of the Sacred Kaaba, tell us — is there someone among you who practices sorcery? Or is there someone present who knows the Greatest Name? For you have rendered us powerless in an instant — our horses cannot move. It has made us unable to plunder you." One of us called back: "There is no sorcerer among us, but there is someone present who knows the Greatest Name!.." "Yes, what you say is true. This cannot be sorcery, but it could be through the Greatest Name, for sorcery could not instill such fear as this. Go now, be on your way!"
We gave thanks to God Almighty, the All-Glorious, and continued on our way.

O you who wander about filled with divine love! These writings of mine have come into your hands. Guard them as dear as your own life, for this is a gift from the Almighty to His servants. If you recognize their worth, act in accordance with their due, conceal them from the eyes of people, and place your trust in my words, you will be able to exercise many powers within this created world (ālem-i kevn u fesād), and among the people of the world [I 328] ...you will become the beloved of hearts. Strive to do this without error! I will now explain to you, one by one, the Quranic verses (Āyāt al-Karima) connected with this purpose — those with nineteen letters. Have no doubt that the Greatest Name (ism Aʿẓam) is contained within them. Believe this. Whoever carries this circle upon himself must be in a state of complete ritual purity.

I have not related this copy in any of the books I have written, for I sought to heed the admonition of Hazreti Ali (may God be pleased with him and honor him). I did not wish its fame to spread abroad. When it comes into your hands, do not broadcast it carelessly either! Whenever you give this circle to someone, do not let him open it and look at its design — hand it over sealed. If the person you give it to is able, let him offer a sacrifice and distribute its meat to the poor.

I had this circle engraved upon a silver plate, and had the Āyāt al-Kursī (the Throne Verse) engraved above the circle, and I carried it upon my person. I persisted in reciting the Asmāʾ (the Divine Names) and the verse after each of the five daily prayers, and by the permission of Allah Most High, I found healing.

O seeker! Into whosever hands these pages come, let him make a vow to the spirit of Hazreti Ali (may God be pleased with him and honor him), in reverence for his power, and fulfill it once his wish is granted — and let him remember this humble servant with a good prayer.

The reason the sacrifice is required is out of reverence for the Divine Names (Asmāʾ al-ilāhiye), and in emulation of the Prophet Hazreti Ibrahim (peace be upon him). The meat of the sacrifice must likewise be distributed to the poor who are in need.

This work of Imam Ghazali (may God be pleased with him) was obtained in the city of Damascus by the dervish Mustafa es-Surizi from a perfect saint; that saint had seen it in the treasury of a sultan named Shahruz Mirza, and copied it in the year 847 of the Hijra.

According to the description given by the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali (may God be pleased with him and honor him), after every obligatory (farz) prayer one first recites the Takbīr ("Allahu ekber" — God is greater) ten (10) times, and then this:
Ferdun Hayyun Hakemun Adlun Kuddūsun.
(The One, the Living, the Judge, the Just, the Holy.)
After the Names (Asmāʾ), one adds the Quranic verse suited to one's purpose, and it must be recited nineteen (19) times.
For example: if you wish to ease a difficult and burdensome matter, after every obligatory prayer first say the Takbīr (Allahu ekber) ten (10) times, then recite this verse:

Add it to the Names and recite it 19 times. The practice must be carried out neither less nor more than prescribed. These Names and this verse are to be recited after every obligatory prayer, nineteen (19) times each, for a period of 19 days.

It must be recited according to the order set forth by Imam Ghazali (may God be pleased with him). For nineteen (19) days, after each of the five daily obligatory prayers, first say the Takbīr (Allahu ekber) ten (10) times, then nineteen (19) times:

In this way, the Junnetul Asmāʾ circle is completed by being written out twice. You keep one copy of the Junnetul Asmāʾ upon your person and soak the other in water; then for nineteen days, after every obligatory prayer, you recite it with the Aya suited to your purpose added to the Names, and on the days of recitation you drink the water for those nineteen days. If, at the end of every nineteen recitations, you recite the Junnetul Asmāʾ prayer once (1), then by the leave of God the Exalted, what you wished for comes to pass.

The rule for making the fourfold wafq: you take the jumal al-kabir value of the Aya to be placed in the wafq and subtract 30 from the total. The remainder is divided by 4. The whole quotient is written into the first cell, and, adding one at each step, you proceed to the last cell to complete the wafq. If the division leaves a remainder of 3, add one extra to the 5th cell; if the remainder is 2, add one extra to the 9th cell; if the remainder is 1, add one extra to the 13th cell — completing the wafq in this manner.
The fourfold wafq belongs to the planet Jupiter, and its day is Thursday. Its celestial angel is Sarfeyail and its earthly angel is Shemhuresh.

[I 361] The Secret of the Seven Letters These seven letters, which do not occur in the Surat al-Fātiḥa, are of exalted worth and lofty standing. Some of these seven letters point to good, and some to evil.

The letter Fe (8): this letter is dry and hot, its nature being fire. Its lunar mansion (manzil) is Eklil. The spirit (rūḥāniyya) of this letter is generally employed in works of good, though its exact nature is not clearly determined. If you use this letter for righteous works in this world, you will attain success, by the leave of Allah, Glorious and Exalted is He.

The letter Jīm ((): this letter is moist and hot, its nature being air. Its lunar mansion is Sureyya. The spirit of the letter Jīm is used for gaining a place among prominent men — for entry among the great, the men of worldly standing, and the men of the pen.
The letter Shīn (<): this letter is dry and hot, its nature being fire. Its lunar mansion is Belde. The spirit of the letter Shīn is of a confused nature and serves none of the affairs of this world.

The letter Se (:): this letter is moist and hot, its nature being air. Its lunar mansion is Sa'dil beli'. The nature of the spirit of the letter Se is temperate (moderate), and it is fitting for every good work.

The letter Ẓāʾ (>): this letter is moist and hot, its nature being air. Its lunar mansion is Feraul muahhir. The nature of this letter's spirit is composite, and it hinders undertakings and endeavours.

The letter Khāʾ (9): this letter is moist and cold, its nature being water. Its lunar mansion is Sa'dil suud. The nature of this letter's spirit is temperate (moderate). It is auspicious and lends aid in every good work.

The letter Ze (+): this letter is moist and hot, its nature being air. Its lunar mansion is Zera'. The spirit of the letter Ze is used for driving away sickness, for the opening of the melekūt (the realm of spirits), and in every work, whether good or evil.

[I 368] The Forty Names It is related from the peerless scholar of his age, the unrivalled savant of his time, he who brought others to perfection, the pole (kutub) of the people of truth, Shihabuddin Suhrewerdi, may his secret be sanctified, that Allah, Exalted is He, gave him forty of His Beautiful Names. There is no son of man who does not stand in need of these Names, which possess many properties. Some of these properties are as follows:

Angels, jinn, men, the heavens, the earths, and everything in the realm of existence are made subservient to these Names. Throughout his entire life the Sheyh never let these Names leave his side. He performed all his wondrous works through the blessing of these Names.

He also enjoined the following: whoever wishes to occupy himself with the prayer of these Names must have a pure heart. He must persevere in reciting it with heart and soul, that he may witness many strange and wondrous things among the works of Allah, and that the secrets of the unseen world (gayb) may be opened to him.
These Names contain such astonishing secrets that, were the seas to become ink, the trees pens, and every created thing a scribe, they could not write out the full commentary on these Names.
When Allah, Exalted is He, wills good for one of His servants, He grants him success in attaining these Names and in reciting them. In the end, astonishing properties are seen in that person.

Shihabuddin Suhrewerdi, may his secret be sanctified, enjoined the following: it is forbidden for those brethren who know these Names to give or entrust them to persons they do not trust or who are unworthy. It is not permitted to put them to trial in unlawful matters. Whoever tests them in what is unlawful, Allah will afflict him with such trouble that he can never be rid of it; on the Day of Judgment, Allah, the Truth, will be his adversary.

Whoever recites these Names must possess piety (takva) and sound belief. He must have no evil habits. He must not be dissolute or a liar. His conduct must be upright and his word true. He should believe in these Names and put them to trial when he has need, and then, God willing, his needs will be met.

After reciting each Name, he fasts for seven days. In the middle of the seven days he recites these Names. Then he will witness astonishing things, as we shall briefly relate under the properties of each Name. It is Allah, Exalted is He, who grants success in what one loves and is content with.
