Whoever continues reciting this blessed name will have the veil of heedlessness lifted from over his heart. God, glorified and exalted, will guide him with the light of guidance, until in the end he can read what is in people's hearts. The polytheism (shirk) in his own heart will vanish, and he will leave this world a muvahhid — one who believes firmly in God's oneness.

If he needs something from another person who will not grant it, he should recite this greatest name (ism Aʿẓam, the Supreme Name) twenty-four times on a Sunday. Whatever he desires will undoubtedly come to pass.

If he wishes to use it on someone else, he should wash, put on new clothes, and recite this blessed name one hundred and twenty times over some food, then feed it to that person. Once that person has eaten it, he will not be able to part from him for even an hour. He will be unable to oppose him in any way, and will lose all patience and resolve where he is concerned. This must be recited with sound and correct belief. It is mujerrep — tried and proven by experience. It is God who grants success in what He loves and is pleased with.
Second Name
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 369

The special property of this name is this: if a person is poor and lowly, without standing or respect among people, and occupies himself with this blessed name, reciting it fifteen times a day, in a short time he will become someone of worth, distinction, and influence. His provision will grow abundant, and everyone who sees him will love him. For the rest of his life he will never again be poor or lowly. He will become a man of dignity among people, and everyone who sees him will hold him in respect, by God's leave and through the blessing of this great name. This is mujerrep. It is God Almighty who grants success in what He loves and is pleased with.
Third Name
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 369
(O Allah, the Praised in all His deeds)

[I 370] The special property of this great and blessed name is this: whoever performs the ritual bath (gusul) at the time of the Friday prayer, puts on new clothes, goes to the mosque, and, once the prayer is finished, recites this blessed name two hundred times where he stands, with sincerity and firm belief — if it should cross his mind, by God's leave, that the earth be folded up for him, this will come to pass by God's leave. And if he wishes to bring forth clouds, or thunder, or lightning, that too will happen. Such a person must harbor no envy, rancor, or hatred in his heart toward his Muslim brothers. It is God who grants success in what He loves and is pleased with.
Fourth Name
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 370
(O Most Merciful over all things and their Bestower of Mercy)

Commentary: The special property of this blessed name is this: if a man's temperament is bad — quick to anger, arrogant, and proud, so that he torments everyone and his deeds are evil, and he lacks the strength to abandon them — let him write this blessed name with musk and saffron, and write his own name together with his mother's name on a piece of white silk cloth, then bury it in a clean place. Before long his character will grow gentle, and his evil deeds will turn to good ones.
If you wish for someone to love you and never part from you for even an hour, fast for three days and recite this blessed name five hundred times each day
Fifth Name
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 370
(O the Living, when there is no living thing, in the everlastingness of His dominion and His subsistence)

Commentary: The special property of this blessed name is this: if a person falls ill and grows weak, his illness worsening until the physicians are helpless to treat him and no medicine has any effect, let this blessed name be written with musk and saffron in a new vessel, dissolved in rainwater, and given to the sick person to drink. Once he drinks it, he will recover by God's leave. And if he drinks it while still in good health, for the rest of his life [I 371] he will never fall ill again, through the blessing of this name. It is God who grants success in what He loves and is pleased with.
Sixth Name
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 371
Yā Kayyūmu felā yefūtu shey'un min ilmih.
(O the Self-Subsisting Sustainer, from whose knowledge nothing escapes)

Commentary: The special property of this great name is this: if a man's heart grows dull, so that no learning remains in his mind and he forgets everything he reads, let him recite this blessed name every day twenty-seven times, taking care to recite it after the dawn prayer. Then his heart will be illuminated, so that everything he has ever heard, from childhood to old age, will come back to his mind, and he will never forget it again. Much will be unveiled to him from the unseen world.

If a person has lost something, let him choose a Monday. When the Sun is in the sign of Aries, let him recite this blessed name one hundred and twenty times with that purpose in mind. He will see the object and its location in his dream. If someone has stolen it, he will see that person in his dream as well. And if he recites it for some other purpose, that too will come to pass.

If someone recites it in his house, nothing will ever be stolen from that house. No thief will ever enter that house again, and no calamity or discord will be seen in it. By God's leave, nothing will be stolen from that house. It is God who grants success in what He loves and is pleased with.
Seventh Name
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 371
(O the One, the Everlasting, the First of all things and their Last)

Commentary: The special property of this blessed and great name is this: if a man has a melancholic temperament, so that evil thoughts constantly pass through his mind, wicked notions occupy him at every moment, and he sinks now and then into dark fancies — so much so that disorders appear in his mind, he grows fearful for his possessions, loses his sleep, and can find no peace — then when he recites this blessed name a great deal, all these fancies and everything else of the kind will leave him.

If he has a powerful enemy, let him recite this blessed name fifty times. His enemy will come to love him and treat him with the affection of a brother. His enemy will not be able to overcome him; no magic will work upon him, and, God willing, nothing evil will be able to harm him. It is mujerrep.

[I 372] Eighth Name Commentary: The special property of this blessed name is also this: if a man is inconstant, occupying himself in all his affairs with vain and worthless things, he must perform a complete ritual ablution (abdest) and pray two rak'ahs with the intention of steadfastness, then fast for three days and recite this blessed name three hundred times. God Almighty will grant him whatever steadfastness he desires.

If he is a sultan, an emir, or someone of similar rank, and he too desires steadfastness in his affairs, let him have this blessed name engraved on the bezel of a silver ring on the twenty-seventh night of Ramadan. The one who engraves the writing must be in a state of ritual purity. He must never take the ring off his finger. He will then become steadfast, and no enemy will ever overcome him. It is God who grants success in what He loves and is pleased with.
Ninth Name
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 372
(O the Eternal Refuge, without likeness — there is nothing like unto Him)

Commentary: The special property of this blessed and great name is this: if a person is given to immorality and sin and lacks the strength to give it up, let him pray with this blessed name. The method of prayer is to choose the day of Jupiter (Mushtarī) — that is, Thursday. He fasts for three days, reciting this blessed name one thousand times each day. God Almighty will make all immorality and sin appear repugnant to him, so that such thoughts never occur to him again and he never looks back at any of it. During these days he must not eat meat, and he must avoid anything unlawfully earned.

If discord arises between husband and wife, day and night, without cause, let him write this blessed name inside a glass vessel, pour in spring water or well water, and give it to the couple to drink. By God's leave, they will never quarrel again.

If he writes this blessed name with musk and saffron on gazelle-hide, wraps it in oilcloth, places it in a cup, and gives it to people who are asked not to quarrel with one another to drink, then, by God's leave, there will never again be strife between them. It is God who grants success in what He loves and is pleased with.
[I 373] Tenth Name
(O the Most Kind — nothing draws near His equal, and there is no way to describe Him)

Commentary: The special property of this blessed name is this: if a person wishes to silence the mouths of others, let him take three miskal of lead — a miskal being a small unit of weight — and make a tablet from it. Let him engrave this blessed name upon it, place it inside the belly of a fish, and bury it in a damp place. Let him write the names of his adversaries on that tablet. Then their tongues will be bound: they will say nothing about him, either to his face or behind his back. His enemies will become friends and will not depart from his word.

If he continues reciting this name for forty-one days, reciting it one thousand times, God will make subservient to him those whose names are written on that tablet, and they will see to all his needs. During these days he must not eat meat, or else he will come to ruin. It is God who grants success in what He loves and is pleased with.
Eleventh Name
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 373
O the Great — You are He) (whom minds cannot fathom in describing His majesty

Commentary: The special property of this blessed name is this: if a sultan or officials harbor ill will toward this person, even to the point of wishing to kill him, let him pray with this name. The method is to fast for seven days, reciting this name one thousand times each day. He will then overcome his enemies — provided he does not stop reciting it. And if he continues to recite it always, the good and blessing of his household will increase.

If a person is burdened with heavy debt and occupies himself with reciting this blessed name, God Almighty will grant him the means to pay off his debt and will give him provision beyond reckoning. It is God who grants success in what He loves and is pleased with.
Twelfth Name
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 373

Commentary: The special property of this blessed name is also this: if a person has been bewitched or struck by the evil eye, let him engrave this blessed name upon a tablet made of seven metals. Then the spell upon him will be broken.
[I 374] By God's leave, the sorcery will be undone. Whatever illness he has, such as vitiligo or leprosy, will be lifted from him.
If he recites this name still more, God will lift every illness from him. It is God who grants success in what He loves and is pleased with.
Thirteenth Name
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 374
(O the Pure, the Undefiled, free from every affliction, for His holiness)

Commentary: The special property of this blessed name is this: if you wish to put it to the test, perform the ritual bath on a Wednesday, put on new clothes, and sit alone in a house where no one else is present. Recite this blessed name one thousand and fifty-one times. During the days of recitation, let there be no immorality or wickedness in your heart. If, by the time you finish reciting, your inward state is pure, seven pure spirits will enter into you. Their sign is that they wear green garments, and on their heads they wear caps like Turkish takkes. They will come and stand before you. They will not speak to you, and you must not speak to them either. Continue occupying yourself with reciting this blessed name until they speak to you. They will say to you: O servant of God, whatever important need you have, let us settle it for the sake of this blessed name. God accepts their wishes at once. May God be pleased with you and with us.

O servants of God, just as you have obeyed this blessed name and come at my summons and request, so too, by the power of this name, help me wherever I may be. Protect me from the evil of friend and foe alike. Should I have a need, fulfill it by God's leave.

During these days one must not eat any meat, and before beginning to recite, one's inward state must be pure — otherwise there is fear of coming to ruin. Your tongue will be seized and you will be unable to speak, and you will not attain your purpose. You must be wary of these spirits, so that no delusion or illusion settles over you. Do not fear the spirit-beings, or their horsemen and footmen. They will come to you in the form of mounted soldiers. A bond will form between you; friendship will be established. If they answer your call and meet your need, summon them again. If they answer your call and greet you, rise to your feet when you see them, and treat them with humility. If they give you their word, rise at once, place your hand upon your chest, and say: "Just as you have honored and shown me respect, may God honor and increase your honor as well. Let there be a sign between us, so that I may call upon you whenever I need to." They will say to you: "Whenever you have a need, we will come to you." You, in turn, step forward and say, [I 375] "my purpose is only that you answer my call whenever I have need." When they hear this request, they will give you a seal white as an egg, with green writing upon it. Take it and kiss it, and touch it to your head and your eyes. Say: "Teach me the special property of this blessed seal." When the summoning is complete and the purpose achieved, anoint it with fine perfumes. Do not let anyone in a state of menstruation or ritual impurity touch this seal. When its task is done, treat them with humility, and say to them: "Return to your places in well-being and safety. Should I have need, I will summon you again." Never neglect to apply fine perfume; then lasting affection will remain between you. Should you have a need, recite this name a few times, and by God's leave they will appear beside you.
O you who desire these things, strive always to remain in a state of ritual ablution, for this blessed name is of great benefit. It is God who grants success in what He loves and is pleased with.
Fourteenth Name
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 375
(O the Sufficient, the Bestower of

Abundance, who enriches what He has created through His gifts and bounty) Commentary: The special property of this blessed name is this: if one person needs something from another, and the other withholds it and a long time passes without the need being met, let him write this blessed name with musk and saffron on tanned gazelle-hide, and bury it at the threshold of the house of the one whose help he needs. His need will be met before long. God Almighty, out of His grace and generosity, will bestow great favor upon him. Blessing will come into his affairs, so that even if he takes a handful of earth, it turns to gold. If he is poor or destitute and in need, let him choose an auspicious day — that is, wait for the day when the Moon is in the sign of Aquarius. Let him write this blessed name on a sheet of paper, wrap it in oilcloth, and drop it into the cup or waterskin from which he drinks. He should do this at a favorable time so that, by God's leave, he may see good and blessing. Then he will see many lights and wondrous things among the workings of God. It is God who grants success in what He loves and is pleased with.
Fifteenth Name
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 375
(O the Immaculate, free from all

injustice, neither approving of it nor party to it) The special property of this blessed name is this: if a tyrant has set upon a person and he cannot escape him, let him recite this blessed name a great deal — [I 376] so much so, a thousand times a day or more. The reason for reciting it so often is that this name is called the ism Aʿẓam, the Supreme Name. Through the blessing of this name, he will be delivered from that tyrant's hand — even if he is in prison, he will be freed. Let him recite this name morning and evening. God will grant him safety, and will give him so much wealth that he will need no one.
Whoever recites this name must be in a state of ritual ablution, and his belief must be sound.
Sixteenth Name
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 376
(O the Most Compassionate, You who have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge)

Commentary: The special property of this blessed name is this: if a person's heart and tongue become bound, so that he is bewildered in his affairs, held in contempt in people's eyes, and whatever work he undertakes he cannot finish or bring to a good outcome, let him occupy himself with this blessed prayer for forty days.

The method is this: during this time he must not eat meat. He should eat rice with shirik oil, and black grapes with the seeds removed, into which he puts a little musk. He must not eat much. He must not sit among other people, but withdraw into seclusion (khalwa), occupying himself with this name day and night, gathering his heart and spirit together. By God's leave he will witness wondrous things.
In the first week he will see signs from the unseen world. There are seven kinds of such signs.
The first: if a week or more passes and he recites still more, he will see the whole of creation laid out before his eyes. His words must always be of God, and his heart must be sincere.

The second: on the eighth day, while in seclusion, two figures from among the spirits will come to him. They will say to him: "What is the purpose of this prayer? Occupy yourself with something else — there is no harm to you in it." Do not answer them under any circumstance. Do not engage with them. Recite this blessed name aloud; if they hear it, they will vanish and go away. Do not fear them — if you fear them, you will come to ruin.

The third sign: on the thirteenth day, prepare a clean house and wait for the appointed times. A bird green like the legendary huma bird will come to you and perch on your head. It will disturb you with its harsh cry and strike you with its wing. Still more birds of this kind will come. Do not fear them; continue reciting aloud. When they see that you persist in reciting this name, they will rise and depart. Do not fear them — let your heart remain steady.
The fourth sign: on the seventeenth day, if he continues occupying himself with this method of prayer, in seclusion after the afternoon prayer he will see people dressed as paupers.
[I 377] Among them will be one wearing patched clothing. His sign is that he is young.

He has a large mole on his right cheek. When he enters through the door of the cell, he will greet you. You must rise for him and return his greeting. This figure will sit beside you and speak a great deal. You must not engage with him and must not let it interrupt your prayer. When he sees that you will not engage with him, he will rise and leave.

The fifth sign: on the twenty-seventh day, whoever passes by you, whether jinn or human, you will unfailingly know their inner state; you will read them and become fully aware of the secret within their hearts.
The condition for this is to keep this secret, which is between you and God, telling no one until the prayer is complete.

The sixth sign: on the twenty-eighth day, draw a square line and sit in the middle of it. Occupy yourself with reciting this blessed name. When night falls, light a green torch and place a large wick in it. Fill the torch with jasmine and fragrant olive oil. Do this for seven nights. Then seven or four spirits (nefs) will come and stand before him. They will say to him: "O servant of God, rise and step outside the line. Whatever you wish, we will do it. If your purpose is that you have fallen in love with someone, we will bring that person to you. If you fear an enemy, we will destroy him. If you desire knowledge, we will teach you. Whatever important matter you have, we will accomplish it all." He must answer them, saying: "O servants of God, leave me — I have no business with you," and continue reciting this blessed name. Whenever they tell him to step outside the line, he must not rise from his place or heed their words. Whenever he hears such a thing from them, he must continue reciting this blessed name until the forty days are complete. At the end of the forty days, he will see a great many things in seclusion. A vast multitude will appear. If it is night, he will see torches, lamps, and candles; if it is day, he will see soldiers. Each will appear in a different form, their weapons and mounts unlike one another. That person must continue reciting this blessed name and be ready for the appointed hour. While he is in this state, he will see a great crowd, among whom is a king. The king rides a beast and holds a serpent as his whip. Around him are many men bearing gold and silver platters, upon which are various jewels. Thirty thousand spirits are under his command. When the possessor of this blessed name arrives, the king greets him. He must rise for him, place his hand upon his head, and receive his greeting with his heart. He must say nothing beyond this, and continue reciting this name. At last the king will say to him: "O servant of God, what is your purpose in reciting this ism Aʿẓam? Whatever needs you have, let us see to them all." He must answer him and say: "O sultan of spirits, may God be well pleased with you from the earth to the sky. My wish is that you place me at the head of your soldiers, so that whenever I have a need they will attend to it and help me. Whatever I ask of them, [I 378] they will fulfill it, by God's leave. And you, O king, do not vanish from my sight even for an hour." Then the king accepts his words. He places him at the head of the army. Both the king and his soldiers obey him. After this he will witness many strange and wondrous things. The spirits will obey him in all important matters, and people will come to depend on him. The special properties of this blessed name are too numerous to recount; we have described them here only in brief.
Seventeenth Name
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 378
(O the Bestower of Grace, Possessor of Kindness, whose favor has encompassed all creation)

Commentary: The special property of this blessed name is this: if a person is burdened with heavy debt and cannot pay it, and he recites this blessed name a great deal, God Almighty will grant him ease in paying it and open for him easy doors of provision. In a short time he will see wondrous things. He will become known among people for the soundness of his character. Whoever sees him will honor him through the blessing of this name.

If he writes this name on paper while the Sun is in the sign of Aries and carries it with him, he will never in his whole life be in need of anyone. By God's power, he will never fall ill. It is God who grants success in what He loves and is pleased with.
Eighteenth Name
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 378
O Judge of His servants, before) (whose awe and desire everyone stands humbled

The special property of this blessed name is this: if someone has worldly wealth and wishes to entrust it to a person he fears may betray that trust, let him write this blessed name with musk and saffron on a piece of white silk, place the trust upon his own head, and then entrust it to the person he fears might betray him.

If he writes this blessed name with earth from the Kaaba and places it in a grave, the body lying there will not decay. If someone has an illness such as vitiligo — God forbid — and he writes this blessed name and carries it with him, by God's leave that illness will depart.

If a person wishes to set out on a journey and his companions will not agree to it, let him write this blessed name and place it in a hole in a wall facing the qibla; his companions will then become content with him and [I 379] ...they take him along on their journeys and give him goods. If there are bandits on the road and he fears for his merchandise, he places this blessed name inside his goods; by God's permission, they will be unable to take anything from him. Its condition is that it be written on gazelle skin with musk and saffron. It is God who grants success in that which He loves and is pleased with.
Nineteenth Name:
(O Creator of all who are in the heavens and the earth, unto Whom all things return.)

The property (hassa) of this blessed and great name is this: if a man has gone missing and no word of him can be had, and one wishes to know where he is, one recites this blessed name five thousand times with a pure intention, glorifying the name of God Most High, and performs two rak'ahs (units of prayer), reciting the Fātiḥa once and the Surah al-Ikhlāṣten times in each rak'ah. Afterward one fasts for three days. One writes this blessed name on gazelle skin and places it beneath one's bedding. That night one sees the missing man in a dream — he may even relate his whole story to him — and by God's permission he returns to his homeland.
Twentieth Name:
(O Merciful One to every one who cries for help and every one in distress, his succor and his refuge.)

The property of this blessed name is this: if a person falls in love and loses sleep and composure, and can find no way to be united with the one he loves, he writes this blessed name with musk and saffron, writing his own name, his mother's name, the beloved's name, and the beloved's mother's name. As he casts it into flowing water, he prays thus: "O God, so-and-so despises me. You know what I desire. I ask You that they love me, so that their flesh mingle with my flesh and their blood with my blood." Then the beloved loses all patience and composure — even if her feet were bound, she would break the bond and come running. The purpose is achieved. By God's permission, the fruit of the garden into whose water the paper is cast increases every year.
Twenty-first Name:
(O Perfect One, whose majesty, dominion, and glory in their fullness no tongue can describe.)

[I 380] The property of this blessed name is this: whoever occupies himself with the invocation of this blessed name will see wondrous things. The method is this: one fasts for twelve days, eating nothing of animal origin, and recites this blessed name two thousand and twenty-five times. Then he becomes a person of standing before kings and sultans; people show him respect, and God Most High eases every difficult matter for him. It is God who grants success in that which He loves and is pleased with.
Twenty-second Name:
Ya mubdial bedai-ia lam tebgha fi inshaiha avnen min halkihi.
(O Originator of wonders, who sought no aid from His creation in bringing them into being.)

Commentary: The property of this blessed name is this: if a person wishes to learn some branch of knowledge but cannot master it, he recites this blessed name ninety-nine times every morning, and God opens the door of the unseen to his heart. This is so even if he has never in his life studied anything. Whatever branch of knowledge he takes up, God eases his mastery of it for him, and reveals to him many insights. By the blessing of God and of this exalted name, he attains what he hoped for. It is God who grants success in that which He loves and is pleased with.
Twenty-third Name:
Yā allāmel guyūbi felā yefūtu sheyun min hifzihi wa lā yeūduh.
(O Knower of all that is hidden, from whose keeping nothing escapes and whom nothing wearies.)

Commentary: The property of this blessed name is this: whoever occupies himself with the invocation of this blessed name and recites it a thousand times will find happiness and blessing hastening to him. He becomes renowned among the people and is gifted with great intelligence — so much so that were the reckoning of the whole world given over to him, he would not, by God's power, be confused by it.

The master of this name, a man of true realization, an ascetic and devout worshiper, the peerless scholar of his age and a master of the age without equal, Shihabuddin Maktul, says: whoever recites this name, even if he knows nothing of writing, will learn it; God grants him a sharp mind and intellect. And if anyone should wish to harm him, do him some evil, or kill him, God turns that person's scheme back upon his own head.
Twenty-fourth Name:
(O Forbearing One, full of

gentleness, whom nothing among His creation equals.) [I 381] Commentary: The property of this blessed name, too, is this: whoever commits it to memory and continues to recite it, no one will be able to argue against him or bring him low; his word will be heeded. If he has a beloved who despises him, he recites this blessed name a thousand times over something to be smelled or eaten, and gives it to the one he loves. It is feared that when she smells or eats it she will go mad with love for him. If he cannot get her to eat it, he writes this blessed name on hatai paper (a fine ornamental paper), writing on it the names of the beloved and her mother, and places it somewhere elevated. It has a powerful effect on her, and by God's permission she comes running to him. It is God who grants success in that which He loves and is pleased with.
Twenty-fifth Name:

Commentary: The property of this blessed name is this: if a person's fortunes decline, he is driven far from his homeland, his wealth is lost, and he is baffled in all his affairs, he recites this blessed name three hundred and one times after the afternoon (ikindi) prayer, counting every occasion of reciting it as a windfall. In a short time his condition improves, and by the blessing of the name he becomes happy.

If he wishes to engage in trade, he continues reciting this blessed name; he prospers in his trade and comes to possess great wealth, and by the blessing of this blessed name he becomes happy — so much so that he can no longer keep count of his own wealth. His standing rises; his name becomes known among the people; he becomes honored and esteemed.

This name is called "the covenant of supreme glory." Whoever recites it must have sound belief, or else his ruin is to be feared. It is God who grants success in that which He loves and is pleased with.
Twenty-sixth Name:
(O Praiseworthy in His acts,

Who bestows favor upon all His creation by His very word.) Commentary: The property of this blessed name is this: whoever desires the increase of his wealth and his servants, and that everyone become dependent upon him, and that he be accepted in God's sight, should continue reciting this blessed name night and day without ever growing weary of it. Whenever he stops reciting it, it is to be feared that he will meet ruin, that his condition will decline, and that he will be held in contempt in the eyes of the people. The master of this name has given it [I 382] the title "the name of return" (ric'at ism). It is God who grants success in that which He loves and is pleased with.
Twenty-seventh Name:

Commentary: The property of this blessed name is this: whoever recites it often, keeps himself apart from other people, and carries it upon his person gains standing among the people. He will be neither humbled nor poor; and if a poor man continues to recite it, he soon acquires great wealth. The method for this is to eat nothing of animal origin during these days, continuing the recitation for twenty-five days, reciting it three thousand two hundred times every day and breathing upon it. He speaks no ill of people, meddles with no one, and talks little. In the end God grants him fortune and happiness, and lifts the veil of heedlessness from his heart, so that he sees wondrous and strange things and can read what is in people's hearts. By the blessing of this name, light shines upon his face. It is God who grants success in that which He loves and is pleased with.
Twenty-eighth Name:
,O Subduer, of mighty force)
.(whose vengeance none can withstand

Commentary: The property of this blessed name is this: this name serves for both love and enmity. In matters of love it has, along with other effects and bindings, some three hundred and sixty properties; we pass briefly over the less fitting of them, lest the commentary grow too long.

[I 405] The Explanation and Properties of the Names of Barhatiyya These exalted names, known as the Barhatiyya, possess many properties and subtle secrets. The learned have named and spoken of the
Barhatiyya as the greatest covenant, the sublime pact, the hidden mystery, the concealed treasure, and the substance that makes gold.

Just as Suleyman ibni Davud's (peace be upon him) vizier Asaf ibni Berhiya, and the sage Kalfetiryus, drew benefit from the Barhatiyya, so too have many scholars and gnostics made use of this priceless treasure, full of hidden secrets.

Jinn, ifrits, marids, and devils can neither rise up nor stand against these blessed names, whose blessing and power are exceedingly sublime. Whoever holds this Qasam (oath-formula) attains success in every working, whether for good or for ill — bringing down an angel, summoning a helper-spirit, fetching, sending, causing possession, overpowering, concealing a thing or bringing it to light, and the like. Whoever attains the secret of this Qasam no longer has need of any other Qasam or ʿAzīma. And whoever lacks knowledge of the Barhatiyya has incomplete knowledge, for the Barhatiyya is the head and the foundation of the spiritual sciences.

When you are about to perform an invocation, purify your clothing and your body, and in a state of ritual purity, in a clean place, at any hour, perfume the place where you are with a fragrant incense (bakhūr). Place a mirror, or a glass bowl filled with pure water, in the hand of a skilled seer. Cover the head of the person who is to look, down to the eyes, with about a meter of white cloth. When you begin the invocation, whichever servant-spirit (khuddām), spiritual king, or both classes together you have invoked, they will answer your call. The seer sees the one invoked, and through him you may ask what you wish and receive the answer. You gain mastery over the spiritual beings, and your word becomes binding upon them. May Allah the Exalted strengthen us all with a spirit from Himself.
The Berhetiye consists of 28 names, equal in number to the letters of the alphabet and to the mansions of the moon. Each name has its own letter and its own mansion.
The first name is Berhetihin; its letter is Alif, and its mansion is Shartayn. Its meaning in Arabic gives it [I 406] these as its noble names. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:

For an easy childbirth: write this noble name 35 times on a clean white plate, wash the writing off with water, and if this water is given to a woman in difficult labor to drink, she will give birth easily by the leave of Allah, the Almighty and Glorious.

For sustenance: if a person struggling in poverty and hardship recites this noble name 100 times a day without interruption for 40 days, before the 40 days are complete that person's provision increases. They come into wealth and abundance, their prosperity and well-being grow, they secure their livelihood with ease, and they grow rich and respected among people.

To strengthen the memory: if a person of weak memory writes this noble name on their right palm 7 times and licks it each morning on an empty stomach, continuing for 7 days, they will retain everything they hear. They will never again forget what they have heard, and their memory will grow very strong by the leave of Allah, the Almighty and Glorious.
The second name is Keririn; its letter is Be, and its mansion is Butayn. Its meaning in Arabic is:
Ya Allāhu illā hu kulli shayʾin (O Allah, there is no god but He, [Lord] of all things) — these are its noble names. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:
To see jinn: whoever recites this blessed name 100 times every night will, in a short time, see jinn with their own eyes. They will even obtain a servant-spirit (khuddām) from among the jinn.
To protect belongings: if this blessed name is written on a piece of paper 11 times and placed among one's belongings, those belongings will not be stolen by a thief, nor come to any harm.

For eye pain: if this noble name is written 17 times on a clean plate, the writing washed off with pure water, and the aching eyes bathed with this water for 3 days, the pain will pass by the leave of Allah, the Almighty and Glorious.

For love: after writing the names Berhetīhin and Karīrin on something edible with your saliva, and reciting these two [I 407] names 100 times over it, if you feed it to your maṭlūb (the target of the working), your love and affection will take a seat upon the heart of the one who eats it.
For love: if you recite the names Berhetihin and Keririn 33 times over a glass of water and give this water to your maṭlūb to drink, your maṭlūb will love you with a most violent passion.

For a girl who cannot marry: if the names Berhetīhin and Karīrin are engraved upon a piece of amber and worn by a girl whose fortune in marriage is closed and who cannot find a husband, she will marry in the shortest time.

For goods that will not sell: if the names Berhetīhin and Karīrin are written on a piece of paper and placed upon goods that will not sell, they will, by the leave of Allah, sell at a high profit in the shortest time.
The third name is Tetlihin; its letter is Jīm, and its mansion is Sureyya. Its Arabic equivalent gives these as its noble names. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:
Against bedbugs: if this noble name is written 13 times on a board and the board hung in a place infested with bedbugs, the bedbugs will move away from there by the leave of Allah the Exalted.
For wealth: whoever recites this noble name 70 times every day will never die without having become wealthy. Allah the Exalted grants abundant provision and livelihood to the one who recites it.

For discord between husband and wife: a man at odds with his wife who writes this noble name 70 times on gazelle skin with musk and saffron, wears it upon his head, and recites the name 70 times every day, will find his wife returning to him with intense affection, never to rebel against him again.

Relations with spirits: whoever adopts the names Berhetīhin, Karīrin, and Tatlīhin as a daily litany (wird) and recites them every day will, in a short time, [I 408] affect the higher and lower spirits and see them with their own eyes.
The fourth name is Turanin; its letter is Dal, and its mansion is Deberan. Its Arabic equivalent is:
Ya hayyu Ya muhyī (O Living, O Life-Giver) — these are its noble names. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:

For protection against evils: write this noble name 5 times on a piece of paper, the last four noble verses of Surah al-Hashr once, the letter He 3 times, and the letter Hemze-Alif 7 times; whoever carries this amulet (ḥirz) upon them will be secure from the evil of jinn, of men, and of tyrants, and will be protected from every kind of evil.
If you wish to take revenge upon a tyrant who has wronged you

If this written paper is hung upon a bewitched or bound person, the sorcery is broken, or if they are bound, the binding is released, and they are healed.

The Exalted Occult Properties of al-Asmāʾ al- Ḥusnā (the Most Beautiful Names of God)
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. II, p. 50

The name of the Essence of God Almighty is the name "Allah." Besides this name, there are ninety-nine attributes mentioned in the Noble Qur'an, and all of these together are called the "al-Asmāʾ al-Ḥusnā" (the Most Beautiful Names). The noble name "Allah" gathers all of these names within itself.
In a hadith narrated by Ebū Hureyre (r.a.), our Prophet, Hazreti Muḥammad (s.a.v.), said:
(God has ninety-nine names; whoever counts and recites them shall truly enter Paradise.)
[II 51] The al-Asmāʾ al-Ḥusnā is this:

Huwallahullezi la ilahe illa huwer rahmanirrahim. Elmeliku [II 52] elkuddusu esselamu elmu'minu el muheyminu elazizu eljebbaru elmutekebbiru el haliku elbariu elmusawwiru elghaffaru elkahharu elwehhabu errezzaku elfettahu elalimu elkabidu elbasitu elhafidu errafiu elmuizzu elmuzillu essemiu elbasiru elhakimu eladlu ellatifu elhabiru elhalimu elazimu elghafuru eshshekuru elaliyyu elkebiru elhafizu elmukitu elhasibu eljelilu elkerimu errakibu elmujibu elvasiu elhakimu elwedudu elmejidu elbaisu eshshehidu elhakku elwekilu elkawiyyu elmetinu elkawiyyu elhamidu elmuhsi elmubdiu elmuidu elmuhyi elmumitu elhayyu elkayyumu elwajidu elmajidu elwahidu elahadu essamedu elkadiru elmuktediru elmukaddimu elmuahhiru elevveli elahiru ezzahiru elbatinu elvali elmutealu elberru ettewwabu el Muntekimu elafuwwu erraufu malikelmulku zuljelali welikramu elmuksitu elcamiu elghaniyyu elmughni elmaniu eddaru ennafiu ennuru elhadi elbediu elbaki elwarisu erreshidu essaburu.
(These are the Ninety-Nine Beautiful Names of God, given here in their Arabic transliteration as they are recited.)

When al-Asmāʾ al-Ḥusnā is recited, the vocative "Yā" is placed before each name and "Celle jelāluhu" (Glorious is His Majesty) is added at the end - as in "Yā Rahmān, celle jelāluhu," "Yā Kerīm, celle jelāluhu," and so on.

1. Whoever recites al-Asmāʾ al-Ḥusnā once every day after the morning prayer, without rising from his place or speaking any worldly word, is kept safe until evening from the mischief of Satan, from sudden death, and from every calamity and misfortune; and whoever recites it after the evening prayer is kept safe in the same way until morning.

2. Whoever recites it once or three times every day after the morning prayer becomes honoured in this world and the next. He becomes a person who is loved and respected among people. He is kept safe from the torment of the grave and the fire of Hell, and enters Paradise.
3. Whoever has a wish from God Almighty and recites al-Asmāʾ al-Ḥusnā seven times, morning or night, for seven days, will have that wish granted by God Almighty.

4. Whoever, intending some good wish or purpose, or the removal of some calamity or misfortune that has befallen him, sits after midnight -especially at the hour before dawn - facing the qibla upon his knees, recites al-Asmāʾ al-Ḥusnā forty-one times, and then opens his hands in supplication, will have his purpose brought about by God Almighty.

[II 53] 5. Whoever has a very important wish and desires it to be fulfilled should recite al-Asmāʾ al-Ḥusnā one thousand times, reciting the following invocation ten times at the start of every hundred, and upon completing the thousand recitations state his wish; by God's leave, it will be answered at that very moment.
The invocation to be recited ten times at the start of every hundred is this:

(In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. My Master, admit me into the gardens of Your Names, and into the gate that is veiled by no light and no darkness, by nothing of itself and by nothing outside it. Loose my hands to attain to grace, and grant me the taste of every savour, that I may be Yours in You, and rejoice in You through the sweetness that comes from You - for You are Gentle, Tender, Merciful, Compassionate, and Generous. Whatever mercy God opens to mankind, none can withhold, and whatever He withholds, none can release thereafter; and He is the Mighty, the Wise. And may God's blessing and peace be upon our master Muḥammad, and upon his family and companions.)
6. Whoever wishes for some particular need to be fulfilled should first purify himself well and take ablution, and then, for the sake of God's pleasure, perform a two-rak'ah

The blessed wafq of al-Asmāʾ al-Ḥusnā to be written is this: this wafq is a shining light that gathers within itself every beauty, and it is an ocean of secrets. It contains within it the ninety-nine names of God Almighty, [II 55] and the name of our Prophet Muḥammad (s.a.v.) is included in it as well. Its diagonals and sides are equal. The sum of every side and every row is 3394 - except that the sixth row is one short, and the seventh row is one more.

Some scholars have said: whoever wishes to supplicate God Almighty by the Ism al-Aʿẓam (the Greatest Name) should calculate the numerical value of his own name by the jumal al-abjad (the science of abjad, whereby every letter carries a numerical value) and see which name of God Almighty it corresponds to. It may match one, two, or three of these Beautiful Names.

For someone named Hilāl, the value corresponds to the name Wekīl (*) among the Beautiful Names. For someone named Ali, his name corresponds to God Almighty's name Aliyyu (+7). For a person named Muḥammad, his name corresponds to God Almighty's names Basīt (86) and Wedūd (99).

Recite this as many times as the numerical value of your own name, then at the end recite Surat al-Inshirāḥand offer blessings upon our Prophet, Hazreti Muḥammad (s.a.v.). [II 59] The Occult Properties of Certain Verses the Exalted Occult Properties of the Noble Basmala The exalted sublimity and sanctity of the noble Basmala (the invocation "Bismillāhi'r-Raḥmāni'r-Raḥīm," "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate") has been explained through many sound (sahih) hadiths that have come down to us.

The scholars and saints are agreed that the noble Basmala is the Ism al-Aʿẓam, the Greatest Name. All the prophets who came before, as well as our Prophet, Hazreti Muḥammad Mustafa (s.a.v.), never let the noble Basmala leave their blessed tongues, at any moment.

Concerning the noble Basmala, the zebāni (the angels who guard Hell) have said: "Whoever continually recites Bismillāhi'r-Raḥmāni'r-Raḥīm shall not enter the fire of Hell." Bismillāhi'r-Raḥmāni'r-Raḥīm consists of nineteen (19) letters, and the number of angels appointed over Hell, the zebāni, is likewise nineteen.
In a hadith narrated from Imam Ca'fer-i Sādik, our Prophet, Hazreti Muḥammad (s.a.v.), said:
The first thing the Pen wrote upon the Preserved Tablet (was Bismillāhi'r-Raḥmāni'r-Raḥīm. When you write a book, write the Basmala at its beginning, for it is the key to every book.)

Concerning the noble Basmala, our Prophet, Hazreti Muḥammad (s.a.v.), said: whoever recites Bismillāhi'r-Raḥmāni'r-Raḥīm has four thousand merits recorded for every letter, four thousand of his sins forgiven, and his rank raised by four thousand degrees.
Likewise, in another hadith it is stated: every lawful undertaking not begun with the noble Basmala is "cut off" - deprived of blessing.

Concerning the merit of the noble Basmala, the great scholar Allāme Zurūk (rahmetullahi aleyh) says in his work "Mukaddime": five hundred years before Hazreti Ādem (Alāyhisselām) was created, Bismillāhi'r-Raḥmāni'r-Raḥīm was already written upon his forehead. When the noble Basmala was first revealed to Ādem (a.s.), he said: "As long as my descendants continue to recite the Basmala, they shall be kept safe from torment." Because Hazreti Ādem [II 60] recited the noble Basmala so much, God Almighty accepted his repentance and forgave his sins. After Hazreti Ādem (a.s.), the Basmala was withdrawn and sent down to Hazreti Nūh (a.s.).
Hazreti Nūh (Alāyhisselām) recited the Basmala often aboard the Ark, and it came to rest upon Mount Jūdī. After Nūh (a.s.), the Basmala was withdrawn and sent down to Ibrāhīm (Alāyhisselām).

When Nemrūd placed him upon the catapult to hurl him into the fire, Ibrāhīm (Alāyhisselām) recited the Basmala; God Almighty made the fire cool and safe for him. Then it was withdrawn once more and sent down to Mūsā (a.s.).

Hazreti Mūsā overcame Pharaoh and his sorcerers by means of the Basmala. The noble Basmala was inscribed in Hebrew upon his staff. Mūsā (a.s.) split the sea by the Basmala and destroyed Pharaoh and his army. Then the Basmala was withdrawn again and sent down to Suleymān (a.s.).

When the noble Basmala was revealed to Suleymān (Alāyhisselām), the angels said to him: "O Suleymān! Today your dominion is complete." When God Almighty sent the Basmala down to Hazreti Suleymān, He proclaimed: "Tell your people that whoever wishes to hear God's pledge of safety should come to Suleymān." When they had all gathered, Hazreti Suleymān ascended the pulpit of Hazreti Ibrāhīm and recited the Verse of Safety:
Bismillāhi'r-Raḥmāni'r-Raḥīm.

Everyone who heard it was filled with joy. They said: "We bear witness that you are God's Messenger." By means of the noble Basmala, Suleymān (a.s.) made the jinn, mankind, and the birds obey him; everything over which he recited it obeyed him. Suleymān (a.s.) prevailed over other nations by the Basmala. God Almighty sustained Suleymān's dominion by means of the noble Basmala. The noble Basmala was inscribed upon Suleymān's seal. The Basmala was then withdrawn from Hazreti Suleymān (a.s.) and sent down to Hazreti Īsā (a.s.).

Hazreti Īsā (a.s.) and the disciples were filled with joy through the Basmala. God Almighty said: "O Īsā, do you know which verse has been sent down to you? Bismillāhi'r-Raḥmāni'r-Raḥīm is the Verse of Safety. Recite it much, in every circumstance. Let the Basmala be the opening of your recitation and your prayer. Whoever continues to say it before prayer and before recitation - Munker and Nekir will not frighten him in the grave, his death will be made easy, and the grave will not press upon him. He will attain My mercy and his grave will be filled with light. I shall raise him from the grave with his body and face made white. His scale will be heavy. I shall complete his light upon the Sirat. Thus he will enter Paradise, and it will be proclaimed to him: you have attained happiness and forgiveness." Hazreti Īsā (Alāyhisselām) asked: "Is this reserved for me alone, O Lord?" [II 61] God Almighty replied: "It is reserved for you and for those who follow you, and after you, for Ahmed (a.s.) and his community." The Basmala was inscribed upon the tongue of Hazreti Īsā (Alāyhisselām). While still an infant in the cradle, he spoke through the miraculous power of the Basmala. By addressing his Lord through the miraculous power of the Basmala, he raised the dead. He loosed the tongues of the mute by the Basmala. He healed leprosy and other ailments through the miraculous power of the Basmala. Afterward it was withdrawn from Hazreti Īsā (a.s.) and sent down to our Prophet, Hazreti Muḥammad (s.a.v.).

Because Hazreti Muḥammad (Sallallahu ʿalayhi wa sellem) recited the Basmala so much, our Prophet became a great and glorious opening unto the world. God Almighty swore an oath and said: if a believer recites the noble Basmala over anything, it will be blessed. If anyone of the community of Muḥammad recites it for the sake of some wish, whatever he has wished for will come to pass.

Those who constantly recite the noble Basmala, and who say it at the start of everything, are delivered from hardship and difficulty, both in this world and the next. Whoever recites the noble Basmala often becomes dignified and awe-inspiring in both the higher and lower worlds. Just as the otherworldly benefit of the noble Basmala is great, so too are its worldly benefits very great. It has many manifest and exalted occult properties (khawāṣṣ). The noble Basmala consists of nineteen letters, and its jumal al-abjad value is 786.

1. It has been narrated from Abdullah ibn Omer (r.a.) as follows: whoever has an important wish from God Almighty and desires to attain it should fast on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. When Friday comes, let him purify himself, take a full ablution (ghusl), and go to the Friday prayer. On his way, let him give whatever charity he can. Raḥmāni'r-Raḥīm (In the name of God, the Merciful, the -Compassionate). He besides whom there is no god, the All Merciful, the All-Compassionate, Knower of the unseen and the -witnessed. And I ask You by Your name Bismillāhi'r-Raḥmāni'r .Raḥīm
There is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, who depends on no other being. Neither slumber nor sleep overtakes Him.

"A prayer that begins with Bismillāhi'r-Raḥmāni'r-Raḥīm is never turned away." 2. This blessed hizb (a fixed litany recited in a set pattern) of the noble Basmala was compiled by Sheyh Abdulkadir Geylani, may God sanctify his secret.

If you wish to attain this beauty and be blessed with great spiritual abundance, rise in the last third of the night, perform a thorough ablution, then sit on your knees facing the qibla and recite the Basmala 786 times, and the following noble ṣalawāt (blessing upon the Prophet) 133 times:

times. If you continue this every night, your name will be inscribed among the list of the evliya (saints). Your name will also be recorded among the blessed. Guard well this lofty secret that has been entrusted to you, and strive to persevere in it. If you are unable to wake in the last third of the night, then recite it every day between the sunnah and the fard of the morning prayer, or after the fard of the morning prayer.

And [I ask You] to send blessings upon our master Muḥammad and upon the family of our master Muḥammad, and grant me such-and-such.)

Whoever has any wish at all, if they recite the above hizb of the Basmala 118 times and then pray while stating their wish, will attain what they desire by the leave of Almighty God.

Whoever wishes to perform the service of the noble Basmala should, after purifying himself thoroughly, withdraw into seclusion (khalwa)

in a clean place and, with complete faith and sincere intention, beginning on a Friday or Sunday, fast in austerity (riyada) for seven (7) days. After every obligatory prayer, recite the noble Basmala 2,000 times, and the hizb seven (7) times. At night, recite the Basmala within the hizb 83 times. In this way you will have recited the Basmala within the hizb 118 times in a single day. While reciting, burn incense (bakhūr) of oud, benzoin (cavi), and frankincense (luban). For food, eat only things made from wheat flour, and raisins. At night, put olive oil in the lamp and light it. Before beginning the recitation, write the wafq of the Basmala and carry it upon your head. Write the wafq a second time as well; wash off the writing with water, and drink this water each day at the time of breaking the fast (iftar) throughout the seven days.

You! Continue the invocation of the noble Basmala under these conditions for seven (7) days. When the seventh day comes, an exalted and magnificent angel will appear to you. The angel wears white clothing, a white turban on his head, and before him stand two pillars of light.

He will say to you: "Peace be upon you, O friend of Allah (veliyyullah)." When you see him, rise at once, cross your hands over your chest, and say: "And upon you be peace, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings; may Allah grant you good for answering my summons." The angel will ask you: "O servant of Allah, what do you desire?" You will say to him: "I ask of you a word that will benefit me in this world and the next." He will say to you: "Gladly, and with grace and honor — but there are certain conditions for you." You will ask him: "What is your condition?" He will say to you: "Swear by Allah! Swear never to lie, never to drink alcohol, never to sow discord between two people, and never to speak ill of others behind their backs." You will say to him: "God willing (Inshaallah)," and extend your hand to him. He will extend his hand to you and administer the oath. He will give you a great jewel and say: "Take this jewel into your mouth, suck it, and swallow your saliva." reaching from the Throne down to the earth. Afterward, take the jewel out of your mouth and keep it with you. With it, you will obtain whatever you desire. You! By the leave of Allah Most High, you will become one of the friends of Allah upon whom there is neither grief nor fear.

[II 89] The Sublime Occult Properties of Āyāt Al-kursī Āyāt al-Kursī (the Throne Verse, Qur'an 2:255) is a verse of many properties and lofty mysteries; it protects the one who recites it from evil deeds and keeps him far from base character.
When a person who has committed wrongdoing recites this glorious verse, he finds within himself a spiritual support. The mystery and wisdom of this verse draws him back from wrongdoing and calms him.
The one who recites it finds a way to live with rank and ample means.

When Āyāt al-Kursī descended upon our Prophet, Muḥammad (peace and blessings upon him), seventy thousand angels accompanied it. In another account, forty thousand angels accompanied it. This is to exalt the worth of this noble verse. So you, too, should know the worth of this verse.

The spiritual discipline (riyada) connected with the Āyāt al-Kursī (the Throne Verse) is sound and has been proven by practice, for a prayer made with this noble verse is never left unanswered. Sheyh Ebu'l-Abbas Ahmed bin Ali el-Būnī says: when you wish to work with the Āyāt al-Kursī, first place your trust in Allah, may He be exalted. Make your heart, the place you are in, and your clothing perfectly clean, and purify your intention. Withdraw into seclusion (khalwa) in a quiet place, and keep plenty of ummal incense (henna-flower seed) beside you — bakhūr (incense) eases the working in matters of this kind. Begin this working on a Tuesday, reciting it seventy-two times after every obligatory prayer.

On the first night, an unpleasant sound resembling the braying of a donkey will come from the corner of the seclusion room. Do not be afraid of this sound or let it startle you — those making it have no power over you.
On the second night, at midnight, you will hear a sound like the clatter of horseshoes above the seclusion room. Do not fear or be troubled by this sound either.

At the exact midnight of the third night, three tomcats — one red, one white, and one black — will come in. They enter through the door and leave from the head end of the room. Again, do not fear or be troubled, for they have no power over you: the summons (dawa) you are performing is shielded by the spiritual veil that stands between you, which is the Āyāt al-Kursī itself.

At the exact midnight of the fourth night, light your incense, turn toward the kible (the direction of prayer), and recite your summons. The wall will suddenly split open and a servant (khadim) made of light will enter. Do not fear or be troubled by him either — keep the ummal incense smoking, and continue the same working until the servant who has come greets you.

The servant will say to you: "Esselamu ʿalayka ya veliyyallah" (Peace be upon you, O friend of Allah). You will answer him: "Wa aleykes salām wa rahmetullahu wa berekatuhu" (And upon you be peace, and the mercy and blessings of Allah). The servant will then ask you: O friend of Allah, what do you want of me? You will say to him: I want a servant who will serve me for the rest of my life. He will then hold out a gold ring inscribed with the Ismullahi Aʿẓam (the Greatest Name of Allah) and say: this ring is a firm covenant between you and me. Whenever you wish for me to be present, put this ring on the finger of your right hand, recite the summons three times, and say: (O King Kendiyās, answer me and come).

[II 94] From then on, whatever you desire through this working — tayyi mekan (traversing distance in an instant), walking on water, or similar wonders (kerāmet) — will come to pass by the leave of Allah, may He be exalted. [II 98] Ḥirz Āyāt These Ḥirz Āyāt (Protective Verses) were compiled by His Holiness Ahmed er-Rifāī, may Allah be pleased with him.

They are recited over patients suffering from epilepsy or paralysis for three or seven days. If the Ḥirz Āyāt are also written out and worn on the person of the epileptic or paralyzed patient, then, by the leave of Allah the Exalted, the illness of epilepsy will never again take hold of them, no sorcery will have any effect on them, and they will also be safe from the evil of jinn, devils, and men.

If these Ḥirz Āyāt are written on a piece of paper with musk and saffron, the writing is then washed off with water, and the patient drinks that water, they will find healing by the leave of Allah the Exalted.
Muḥammad bin Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, has said: I recited these Ḥirz Āyāt over an old man who had been struck by paralysis.
He said that by the leave of Allah, may He be exalted, and through the blessing (baraka) of these noble verses, the patient was delivered from that affliction.

Whoever recites these Ḥirz Āyāt and then enters the presence of a cruel tyrant will, by the leave of Allah the Exalted, be kept safe and protected from his oppression, his evil, his harm, and his injury.
Instead of harm from that cruel tyrant, he will receive respect and honor; instead of oppression, he will receive help. The conditions for reciting these Ḥirz Āyāt are as follows.
First perform a proper ablution (abdest), then recite istighfar (a plea for forgiveness) seven times and the ṣalawāt (blessings upon the Prophet)

eleven times. With the intention that the patient recover, recite the Euzu Basmala, Surat al-Ikhlāṣthree times, and Surat al-Fātiḥa once, and dedicate their reward to the spirit of our Prophet, His Holiness Muḥammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and to the spirit of His Holiness Ahmed er-Rifāī.
Recite these Ḥirz Āyāt, together with their prayer, from where you are sitting while turning toward the epileptic person, and breathe over them at the points indicated.

If the epilepsy, paralysis, or colic occurred within the past year, recite it once a day, either in the morning or after the afternoon prayer, for three days. If the illness occurred more than a year ago, recite it twice a day, morning and evening, for seven days. If you also write out the Ḥirz Āyāt and have the patient wear them, the epileptic patient will, by the leave of Allah, may He be exalted, be healed.

Our Prophet, His Holiness Muḥammad, peace and blessings be upon him, has said in a noble hadith: whoever recites these Ḥirz Āyāt, no evil from jinn, man, or beast will touch that person during that day and night. Out of reverence for these noble verses, Allah the Almighty helps that person in every matter, and preserves not only that person but also his property and his children.

[II 112] Verses of Opening (fetih Āyāt)

It has been related on the authority of the Pole of the Gnostics, the Succor of those who attain union, Sheyh Ebu'l-Abbas (may Allah sanctify his secret), that the Prophet Muḥammad Mustafa (peace and blessings be upon him) used to gather together every "Verse of Opening" (fetih āya — a Qur'anic verse built around the root fetih, "to open" or "to grant victory") to be found in the Noble Qur'an, and would recite them continually, morning and evening.
Whenever he entered battle against enemies, unbelievers, and hypocrites, he would recite these Verses of Opening and thereby attain victory and triumph.

Whoever writes these Verses of Opening upon a paper with musk and saffron, and carries that paper upon his person, making a daily devotional practice (wird) of reciting these verses, will be granted complete and unfailing provision by Almighty Allah.
Imam al-Ghazali (may Allah sanctify his secret) says in his work entitled Hawassu'l-Kur'an (The Occult Properties of the Qur'an):
whoever writes these Verses of Opening upon a paper and always carries them upon his person — for that person, Allah Almighty will open every door of good and close every door of evil.

Some of the scholars of the occult sciences (khawāṣṣ) have said: fast for three days for the sake of Allah's good pleasure. On the fourth night, rise toward dawn, perform a proper ritual ablution, and sit facing the qibla. Write these Verses of Opening upon a paper with musk and saffron. Once you have written them, place the paper before you and recite the Divine Name Yā Fettāh (O Opener) one thousand and one times. Then take the paper in your hand and say:
O Allah, O Opener of doors, open) .(for me the best of doors

— then fold the paper once. Continue in this same way until the paper has become a talisman (nuskha). Wrap this talisman in a piece of oilcloth, and for as long as you carry it upon your person, Allah Almighty will open for you every door of good and close every door of evil.
Whoever recites this for any particular purpose must hold a proper license (icazet) from a qualified master in this field. There is great benefit in reciting it once every day.

[II 117] Verses of Sustenance (rizk Āyāt)

Whoever desires that his provision be abundant, his earnings easy, and that people hold him in respect and affection, let him write these Verses of Sustenance upon a paper with musk and saffron. If he carries this written amulet (ḥirz) upon his person and makes a daily devotional practice of reciting it, Allah Almighty will provide for him from a source he never expected. Everyone will love, esteem, and honor him.

Ebu Muḥammad el-Yafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him), the author of the work entitled Ed-Durru'n-Nazim, says the following about the Verses of Sustenance: "I saw it in a document written in the very hand of Sheyh Ebu'l-Abbas el-Mursi, in which he stated: whether these Verses of Sustenance be written, recited, or simply kept upon one's person — by any of these means, whoever keeps these noble verses with him will reach his desired aim, swiftly and powerfully, within the space of a month."
